text:
Bible Study: Hebrews 9–11
Pillar I: The Canonical Benchmark & Historical-Grammatical Context
1. The Historical-Grammatical Setting
The Audience and the Temptation to Apostatize: The Epistle to the Hebrews was written to first-century Jewish believers undergoing severe social ostracism, persecution, and the confiscation of goods (Hebrews 10:32–34). The temptation confronting them was not pagan hedonism, but religious retreat—abandoning their confession in the crucified Messiah to return to the visible, socially accepted, and legally protected Levitical system of the Jerusalem Temple.
The Structural Contrast of Sanctuaries (Hebrews 9:1–10): The author begins by cataloging the furniture and ordinances of the earthly Tabernacle: the candlestick, table of shewbread, golden censer, and the Ark of the Covenant overshadowed by the cherubim of glory. He outlines the dual-compartment structure:
The priests entered the first tabernacle (the Holy Place) daily to accomplish the service of God.
The high priest alone entered the second tabernacle (the Holy of Holies) once every year on the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur), never without sacrificial blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people.
The author provides the inspired, grammatical verdict in verse 8: the Holy Ghost signified that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest while the first tabernacle was still standing, functioning merely as a temporal figure (parabolē) for the time then present.
The Ultimate Blood Covenant (Hebrews 9:11–28): In contrast to the repeated entries of Levitical priests with the blood of bulls and goats, Jesus Christ appeared as the High Priest of good things to come. By His own blood, He entered once (ephapax—once for all time) into the holy place of the true, uncreated heavenly sanctuary, having obtained eternal redemption for us. A legal testament (diathēkē) requires the death of the testator to take effect; hence, under the law, almost all things are purged with blood, and "without shedding of blood is no remission" (9:22). Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many, and to those looking for Him He will appear the second time without sin unto salvation.
The Inefficacy of Shadows vs. The Single Offering (Hebrews 10:1–18): The Mosaic law possessed only a shadow (skia) of good things to come, not the very image (eikōn) of the things. Its perpetual, annual sacrifices could never make the comers thereunto perfect; otherwise, they would have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers once purged would have had no more conscience of sins. Quoting Psalm 40:6–8 ("Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me"), Christ abolished the first system to establish the second. By that will, believers are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. While every Levitical priest stands daily ministering because his work is never done, this Man, after offering one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God (10:11–12).
The Peril of Willful Apostasy (Hebrews 10:19–39): Having boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus via the new and living way consecrated through His flesh (the veil), believers are exhorted to draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith. The author issues a severe warning against deliberate defection back to the Temple system: if one sins willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation. Trampling underfoot the Son of God and counting the blood of the covenant an unholy thing incurs a vengeance far stricter than the death penalty under Moses’ law.
The Forensic Roll Call of Faith (Hebrews 11:1–40): The author defines biblical faith not as blind optimism or mystical feeling, but as the substance (hypostasis—underlying legal reality) of things hoped for, the evidence (elenchos—proof/conviction) of things not seen. He traces the historical ledger from Abel to the prophets, showing that the elders obtained a good report not by ceremonial legalism, but by unwavering trust in God's promises. They lived as strangers and pilgrims on the earth, looking for a city that hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
Pillar II: Deeper Theological Analysis
1. The Decisive Shift from Shadow (Skia) to Substance (Sōma)
The architecture of redemption is linear and non-repeatable. The entire Levitical apparatus—the physical linen curtains, golden altars, animal blood, and priestly vestments—was never designed to be the final answer; it was a divine pedagogical model operating as a legal type.
The Limitation of Animal Blood: Animal sacrifices could cover (kaphar) sin ceremonially and cleanse the outward flesh, but they had zero power to purge the inward conscience (Hebrews 9:9, 14; 10:4). An animal cannot stand as a moral substitute for a human rebel.
The Perfection of the God-Man's Sacrifice: Christ's sacrifice is efficacious because of who He is: the eternal Son who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without spot to God. Because His offering is infinite in value, it does not require repeating.
2. The Posture of the High Priest: Standing vs. Sitting
A key historical-theological detail highlighted in chapter 10 is the furniture of the earthly sanctuary versus the position of Christ in heaven:
In the Tabernacle and Temple, there were no chairs. A Levitical priest was never permitted to sit down during his service; his posture was always standing, constantly offering the same sacrifices which could never take away sins. A standing priest is a visual sign of an unfinished task.
In contrast, Jesus Christ offered one single sacrifice for sins forever, and sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:12). The sitting of the Son is the supreme judicial declaration: the debt is paid, divine justice is satisfied, and the work of redemption is finished forever.
3. The Anatomy of Willful Sin (Hebrews 10:26–29)
Hebrews 10:26 is frequently misunderstood as a loss of salvation due to personal moral stumbling or weakness of the flesh. In its strict historical-grammatical context, the "willful sin" is systemic apostasy:
It is a deliberate, conscious rejection of the blood of the New Covenant in order to return to the animal sacrifices of the Old Covenant.
To turn back to animal sacrifices after the Cross is to declare that Jesus was an imposter, that His blood was as common and unholy as an ordinary criminal's, and to insult the Spirit of grace. Because Christ is the ultimate and final sacrifice, once He is rejected, there is no alternate altar left in existence where a soul can find forgiveness.
4. The Biblical Definition of Faith vs. Mystical Subjectivism
Hebrews 11 demolishes the modern notion that faith is a positive-thinking technique, a tool to manifest wealth, or an internal vibrational state.
Substance (Hypostasis): In Greek commerce and legal documentation, hypostasis referred to a title deed—the underlying physical proof of ownership for property not yet in hand.
Evidence (Elenchos): A legal term for forensic proof brought into a court of law to establish fact.
Biblical faith is taking God at His spoken word and acting upon His covenants despite visible circumstances. Faith does not create reality; faith acts in total obedience to the reality God has declared. The men and women of Hebrews 11 did not escape suffering through positive visualization; they were tortured, stoned, sawn asunder, and slain with the sword because their hope was anchored in the resurrection and a heavenly homeland.
Pillar III: Exemplifying Truth in the Daily Walk
For the seeker auditing truth in daily practice, Hebrews 9–11 establishes three disciplines:
Rest in the Finished Work (Rejecting Modern Sacralism):
The seeker must never attempt to approach God on the basis of personal performance, emotional sincerity, or religious rituals. When guilt assails the conscience, the answer is not self-flagellation or spiritual penance, but looking to the High Priest who is seated at the right hand of the Father. His blood alone cleanses the dead works of human effort to serve the living God (Hebrews 9:14).
Hold Fast the Profession of Faith Without Wavering:
In seasons of cultural hostility, the pressure to conform and retreat into socially acceptable religious forms is immense. Hebrews 10:23–25 commands the believer to hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, provoking one another to love and good works, and refusing to abandon the assembly of the saints. Spiritual endurance is sustained by fixing the eyes of faith on the promise of the coming Deliverer: "For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry" (Hebrews 10:37).
Walk by the Title Deed of God's Word:
Like the patriarchs, the truth seeker must live as a pilgrim in this present world, recognizing that earthbound cities, political movements, and secular empires have no eternal foundations. Faith lives by the ledger of God's written promises, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season (Hebrews 11:25), esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of this world.
Synthesized Message for the Truth Seeker
The testimony of Hebrews 9–11 marks the absolute dividing line between shadow and substance, religion and redemption. The earthly Tabernacle, with its endless blood and standing priests, proclaimed that the ultimate remedy had not yet arrived. But Jesus Christ, entering into heaven itself with His own blood, has forever settled the sin debt of His people and sat down in sovereign triumph.
There is no alternate altar, no secondary sacrifice, and no spiritual back door: to reject the finished atonement of Christ is to invite the unmitigated judgment of the living God. The true seeker does not drift in the shifting currents of religious compromise or emotional mysticism. Grounded in the legal title deed of the written Word, the believer walks as a pilgrim of faith—holding fast the confession of Christ, looking beyond the temporal horizons of this fallen earth, and pressing onward toward that heavenly city whose builder and maker is God.
The Berean Conclusion as to the author:
While strong arguments connect the theology to the apostle Paul (or someone writing under his apostolic oversight), the Holy Spirit intentionally preserved this letter anonymously in the text.
The divine architecture behind this is fitting: because the entire epistle presents Jesus Christ as the ultimate Apostle, Prophet, and High Priest through whom God has spoken in these last days (Hebrews 1:2; 3:1), the human instrument recedes into the background so that the voice of Christ alone commands the reader's attention.

The straight tips did the heavy lifting with Indamouse (Race 1), Miss Dynamo (Race 2) and Gambler (Race 5) pinching the big moments, and the day had that classic Sunshine Coast vibe, slow tempo early, then the race turns into a who-can-run-on-better contest. Bias-wise, if you were in the right run and not doing dumb shit early, you could actually salute, especially when the market lined up with the map.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗜𝘁 𝗨𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗱

The first couple races set the tone straight away. It was that slow to moderate feel you talked about beforehand, so the “sit handy and let ‘em come to you” plan paid rent. Indamouse popped the switch late from a good spot, then Miss Dynamo did exactly what a stayer in a slow grind should do, she travelled in rhythm and got the job done in the straight without needing a miracle.

Mid-meeting it got a bit more swingy, and that’s where you saw why these tracks can humble you. We tried to back the clean lanes with Kings Domain and Raiderlicious, but both each-way shots got exposed once the race didn’t pan out the way we wanted, and the finish did what it always does, it picked the stronger travellers late. Once you hit the back half, straight win shots got punished by positioning and timing, with the winners coming from other runs that were better timed on the day.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗯𝗼𝗮𝗿𝗱

Straight selections netted you a win on the day, and the hits were real. The losses stung, yeah, but it didn’t turn into a bloodbath, it turned into a lesson with receipts.

𝗪𝗶𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀 (𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁-𝗢𝘂𝘁)

- R1 Indamouse — $13.00 Win @ $1.85 → +$𝟭𝟭.𝟬𝟱
- R2 Miss Dynamo — $15.00 Win @ $5.50 → +$𝟲𝟳.𝟱𝟬
- R5 Gambler — $15.00 Win @ $2.90 → +$𝟮𝟴.𝟱𝟬

𝗕𝗶𝗴 𝟯 𝗠𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁

Big 3 Multi HIT. For fun, the payout was $10 for the collect.

𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗯𝘆 𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲 — 𝗛𝗼𝘄'𝗱 𝗪𝗲 𝗚𝗼?

- R1: 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀𝗲 Win — WON (hit the line strong)  
- R2: 𝗠𝗶𝘀𝘀 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗼 Win — WON (slow-tempo grind, perfect late delivery)  
- R3: 𝗞𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝗗𝗼𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 Each Way — Missed (blinkers time and pace profile didn’t click when it mattered)  
- R4: 𝗥𝗮𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 Each Way — Missed (1000m sprint pressure, didn’t get the finish she needed)  
- R5: 𝗚𝗮𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗿 Win — WON (straight-up speed job, no fuss)  
- R6: 𝗥𝗶𝗰𝗸𝘆𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗺𝗯𝗼𝗮𝘁 Win — Missed (ran her race, just not the right one on the day, timing was off)  
- R7: 𝗥𝗼𝘆𝗮𝗹 𝗗𝗶𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁 Win — Missed (couldn’t secure the winning run, others timed it better late)  
- R8: 𝗡𝗮𝘃𝘆 𝗡𝗶𝗻𝗮 Win — Missed (position good enough for a run, but the finish went elsewhere)

Selections: 3/8 hit for +$107.05

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗪𝗲 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱 — 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱

Pace was the whole story, even when it looked boring. When the tempo sat slow-ish, the races rewarded horses that stayed composed, didn’t take early action, and could quicken in the last section without needing the track to save them. Indamouse and Miss Dynamo were both prime examples of “travel well first, then sprint when it counts.”

The market-matching thing mattered too. Gambler was the one that looked like the plain answer and delivered like it, no drama, just the speed when the gaps opened. When we tried to get too clever with each-way types in races that tightened up late, we copped the blunt end of Sunshine Coast sprint physics.

Where we got caught was the razor-thin line between “good run” and “winning run.” In Race 6 and Race 7, the winners were the ones who timed the final burst best, and our straight win picks were a fraction too flat in that last yard, or just landed in traffic when it mattered.

If I had to pick one factor that defined the day, it was timing with the pace. Not early courage, not late hope, timing. The track makes liars out of anyone trying to force it from the wrong pocket.

𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗱 — 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝗽 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗱 𝗢𝘂𝘁

With the rail out (+9m), the track still offered chances, but it wasn’t a magic inside freeway. Early on, the better rides were the ones that respected the tempo, sat in their lane, and came with intent once the leaders started to give ground.

As the day went on, the “race shape approval” stuff held up more than the fancy angles. The closer-and-timed lanes won more often than the early pressure did, and the finish section basically decided everything. If your plan required the horse to do improv at the 600m, the track punished you for it.

Maa Harsiddhi – Illuminating the Darkest Corners of Life 🪔

Jai Maa Harsiddhi! 🙏

In the ancient, time-defying city of Avantika (Ujjain), alongside the holy Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, stands the glowing Harsiddhi Shaktipeeth. This is the sacred ground where Maa Sati’s Elbow fell. The temple is famous for its towering, spectacular pillars of light, holding hundreds of diyas that pierce the night sky. 

Maa Harsiddhi is the ultimate provider of joy, success, and spiritual energy. When the darkness of confusion, stress, or grief tries to settle over your life, Maa steps in to light the lamps of hope within you. Her presence acts like a gentle flame that warms our cold worries and turns them into unwavering faith. You never have to stumble in the dark when Shaktirupe Maa is lighting your path.
Imagine the glowing lamps of Ujjain today and let Her light fill your mind with peace. 🪔

21/51 Shaktipeeth

#Harsiddhi #Ujjain #MadhyaPradesh #Shaktipeeth

The 13th Shaktipeeth: According to the Shiva Purana, the temple is designated as one of the 51 holy Shakti Peethas. It marks the exact spot where the right elbow of Goddess Sati fell to earth during Lord Shiva’s cosmic dance of grief (Rudra Tandava)

The Skanda Purana notes that Goddess Chandi earned the name "Harsiddhi" (She who grants fulfillment and vanquishes all) after successfully destroying the rogue demons Chand and Prachand at the behest of Lord Shiva.

The legendary 1st-century BCE ruler King Vikramaditya revered Maa Harsiddhi as his Kuldevi (clan deity). Folklore dictates that he offered his head at her feet 11 times out of absolute devotion, and each time, the benevolent Mother restored his life.

text:
Maa Ambaji – The Light That Has No Beginning or End🪔

Jai Maa Ambe! 🙏🪔

On the sacred border of Gujarat and Rajasthan, atop the majestic Gabbar Hill, lies the ancient Ambaji Shaktipeeth. This is where Maa Sati’s Heart fell. Incredibly, there is no idol inside the inner sanctum; instead, Maa is worshipped through a holy Viso Yantra, hidden behind sacred drapes. 

Worshipping Maa without a visible form is a beautiful reminder of Her ultimate closeness. She isn't bound by a physical frame; She is the pure, cosmic light that fills the entire universe and flows directly through our souls. Like a mother who holds her child tight in a pitch-black room, you don't need to see Her to know She is there. You can feel Her heartbeat in your own. 

Close your eyes today and feel the unmanifested light of Maa Ambe warming your heart. 🪔 

19/51 Shaktipeeth 
Countdown to Navratri 2026

#Ambaji #GabbarHill #Gujarat #Shaktipeeth

The Ambaji Mata Temple (historically known as the Arasuri Amba Mandir) is a highly revered Hindu temple complex located in the town of Ambaji within the Banaskantha district of Gujarat, India, right near the border of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

Unlike almost every other major Hindu shrine, the garbhagriha (inner sanctum) contains no anthropomorphic statue or painting. Instead, devotion is focused entirely on the Shree Visa Yantra—a sacred geometric diagram etched onto a gilded plate.

The Yantra is so sacred that it cannot be viewed with the naked eye; photography is strictly forbidden. Priests blindfold themselves while dressing the Yantra in traditional attire, artfully creating the silhouette of an enthroned goddess for the devotees to witness during Darshan.

Just 3 km away stands Gabbar Hill, the ancient, original seat of the Goddess. Pilgrims can ascend 999 stone steps or ride a scenic ropeway to see the eternal flame and the footprints of Maa Amba.

text:
Tucker Carlson is an antisemite?

GROK:

Not in the sense of an open racial creed that Jews are biologically inferior, and he rejects the label. A large share of the accusation is about a sustained pattern of conspiracy claims that treat Jews, Jewish organizations, or Israel as a hidden, malevolent force over American policy—claims that go well beyond ordinary criticism of Israel.

Carlson has said he is not an antisemite. At Turning Point USA’s AmericaFest in December 2025, he argued that antisemitism is immoral in his religion because it is wrong to hate people for how they were born, and that Christianity requires judging individuals rather than groups. He also says he is “in no sense obsessed with the Jews,” and often redirects blame onto “Christian Zionists” (Ted Cruz, George W. Bush, Mike Huckabee), whom he has called carriers of a “brain virus” and said he dislikes “more than anybody.”

The case against him is about repetition and framing, not a single slur:

He gave a friendly platform to Nick Fuentes, who has praised Hitler and pushed Jewish-control conspiracies. Carlson complimented him and only gently disagreed with the claim that Jewish loyalty to the U.S. is inherently suspect. The interview split the right; Ben Shapiro and others treated it as mainstreaming open antisemitism, while some (initially Kevin Roberts at Heritage) defended hosting him.

In 2024 he called Darryl Cooper possibly “the best and most honest popular historian in the United States.” Cooper argued that the Holocaust was largely the result of wartime mismanagement rather than deliberate genocide and cast Churchill as the chief villain of World War II. Jewish members of Congress and Yad Vashem condemned the interview.

He has treated “dancing Israelis” and Israeli foreknowledge of 9/11 as “all true.”
In 2026 he linked the Israel–Iran conflict to a Chabad-driven plan to destroy Al-Aqsa and rebuild the Third Temple, with Western countries as the real target. Critics noted this recycles the old “Jews secretly start wars” trope; he offered no serious evidence.

He has claimed Israel is “probably the most violent country on earth” per capita, that Netanyahu believes in “blood guilt” and tried to punish members of Carlson’s family, and that Israeli officials were implicated in Epstein’s orbit on the basis of material later identified as a fake image.

Critics also point to remarks at Charlie Kirk’s memorial that they heard as echoing the deicide charge and hinting at a Jewish role in the killing. 

StopAntisemitism named him its 2025 “Antisemite of the Year” largely for this pattern and for platforming others.

Opposing U.S. aid to Israel, criticizing Netanyahu, or objecting to the Gaza war is not antisemitism. Israelis and American Jews do all of those things constantly. Foreign-policy disagreement, dual-loyalty questions about any ally, and skepticism of lobbying are legitimate topics. 

What moves the argument into antisemitic territory is the cumulative picture: secret ethnic or religious cabals (Chabad, “neocons” as a euphemism), collective blood guilt, 9/11 foreknowledge presented as fact, Holocaust soft-revisionism left largely unchallenged, and a volume of focus that trackers have put at well over a thousand mentions of “Jew” or “Jews” on his shows in a year—while he denies any fixation.

So the accurate description is narrower than the slogan. He is a leading voice of anti-Israel politics on the American right who repeatedly uses classic antisemitic conspiracy structures, platforms people who state the ideology outright, and denies that the pattern means what his critics say it means. Whether that makes the noun “antisemite” the right word depends on how strictly you define it; the underlying record is not seriously in dispute.

Q: We have the '2026-27 BABYMONSTER WORLD TOUR [춤 (CHOOM)]'  in full swing, and we can’t wait to see you in Australia at the end of the year. What other creative plans do you going into next year?

🐰: Going forward, I hope we’ll have more opportunities to develop BABYMONSTER’s identity and show what we have to offer beyond our music. This tour has been really inspiring, from performing on different stages to meeting different audiences in person. We’ve also been talking a lot as a group about what we could improve and how we can make our performances even better.

We hope to bring what we’ve experienced on this tour into our future music and performances and surprise our fans once again. There’s not much we can share yet, but please look forward to what’s next for BABYMONSTER!

Q: I want to go back to 2024 and talk about your single [FOREVER]. This is one of our favourite tracks from you, it has this glorious, uplifting pop feel to it while also retaining an experimental edge with its unusual structure and the change in speed and mood between the sung sections and the rapped sections. Could you tell us what this song means to you, and what you focused on most when bringing it to life on stage?  

🐰: [FOREVER] is a song that really showed me just how much fun being on stage can be. Like you mentioned, it has a bright, refreshing vibe, but there are also rap sections where the mood suddenly shifts. I love that it lets us showcase so many different sides of BABYMONSTER and bring a fresh energy to every performance.

When performing it, I felt that the most important thing was to capture the song’s free-spirited and confident energy. While getting the choreography right is important, I really wanted our genuine enjoyment of performing the song to come through on stage. I think our songs really come alive when we perform them live. In [FOREVER], there’s a moment near the end where the whole crowd sings along with us, and seeing everyone singing and having fun together gives me such an incredible rush of happiness.

#America’s Priorities: Bombing Others, Neglecting Itself

💣 Top Priority: Bombing, Then Counting the Money

The U.S. defense budget reached $886 billion for 2026. What does this figure actually mean?

It exceeds the combined defense budgets of the nine nations ranking immediately below the U.S. It is three times China’s defense budget and ten times Russia’s.

Of that $886 billion, more than half flows to Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, and General Dynamics the five giants of the military-industrial complex.

They do not produce housing. They do not produce medicine. They do not produce food. They produce bombs, missiles, fighter jets, and drones.

These bombs are then shipped to Israel, raining down on children in Gaza. Shipped to Saudi Arabia, striking hospitals in Yemen. Shipped to Ukraine, tearing into the chests of soldiers on both sides.

When bombs explode, Lockheed Martin’s stock price rises. When children die, Raytheon’s quarterly dividends increase. When hospitals are destroyed, Boeing’s CEO collects a bonus.

This is the American business model: lining its own pockets with the blood of others.

🏚️ Second Priority: Homelessness at Home? Not a "Priority"

At the very moment the U.S. was shipping 2,596 consignments of weapons and ammunition to Israel, over 75,000 people in Los Angeles County were homeless.

While the U.S. was supplying bombs to Saudi Arabia to strike Yemen, more than 13,000 people in Seattle were sleeping on the streets.

While the U.S. was deploying aircraft carriers to the Strait of Hormuz, over 171,000 people in California were homeless—the highest number in the nation.

The U.S. spent trillions of dollars overseas "rebuilding" Iraq and Afghanistan. Yet, its own cities are turning into the Third World.  In Los Angeles’ Skid Row, tents stretch endlessly, a city of despair. On Seattle’s Third Avenue, hypodermic needles litter the ground an unending plague. In San Francisco’s Tenderloin, piles of feces and trash serve as a mirror, reflecting the true face of this empire.

And what has the U.S. government done?

It spent billions clearing homeless encampments in Los Angeles not to provide housing, but to drive people away. It spent hundreds of millions increasing police patrols in Seattle not to offer treatment, but to make arrests. It spent tens of millions installing fences in San Francisco—not to restore dignity, but to make the people disappear.

This is not "solving the homelessness problem." This is "solving the homeless people."

💊 Priority No. 3: The CIA’s Drug Trade

While the U.S. government loudly proclaims its commitment to "combating drug trafficking" in public, what is the CIA actually doing?

It is supplying drugs.

This is not a conspiracy theory. It is well-documented history.

◾The 1980s: CIA-backed Nicaraguan Contras smuggled cocaine into Black neighborhoods in Los Angeles, using the profits to fund their war. Journalist Gary Webb’s "Dark Alliance" series exposed this only for him to be demonized by the mainstream media and ultimately driven to suicide.
◾ Afghanistan: Following the 2001 U.S. invasion, Afghanistan’s heroin production skyrocketed from 185 tons to 9,000 tons accounting for 90% of the global supply. During the 20-year U.S. occupation, drug production increased fiftyfold. Who was protecting the poppy fields? Who was protecting the drug lords? The CIA’s allies.
◾Haiti: CIA-backed politicians and paramilitary groups turned Haiti into a transit hub for cocaine. Drugs flowed into the United States, while profits flowed into the CIA’s "black budget."  While the U.S. "fights drugs" at the border, the CIA "manufactures drugs" abroad.

This isn't a "failure." It’s by design.

Drugs have devastated America's impoverished communities Black, Latino, and the white working class. They breed crime, violence, and despair. They keep people who should be organizing to demand housing and healthcare hooked on fentanyl and heroin.

The CIA doesn't need to build internment camps. It just needs to let drugs flow into the community.

☕ Starbucks Leaves Seattle, While Los Angeles Rots

Starbucks the coffee giant that calls itself a "third place" is closing dozens of stores in Seattle. The reason? "Safety concerns."

Translation: too many homeless people, too much drug use, too much crime.

And what about Los Angeles? Democrats have ruled Los Angeles for decades. They control the City Council, the County Board of Supervisors, and the State Legislature. They preach "progressivism," "inclusivity," and "caring for the homeless."

And the result?

◾ Homelessness in Los Angeles has risen by 70% over the last decade.
◾ The median home price in Los Angeles exceeds $900,000.
◾ The average monthly rent in Los Angeles is $2,500.
◾ Los Angeles has one of the widest wealth gaps in the country.

What have the Democrats done?

They’ve allowed Blackstone and speculative funds to buy up thousands of homes and hike the rents. They’ve allowed Airbnb and short-term rental platforms to turn residential homes into hotels. They’ve allowed developers to build luxury condos instead of affordable housing. They’ve allowed police to clear out encampments instead of building housing.

Then they point the finger at Trump and say, "He did it."

No. *You* did it. You run Los Angeles. You hold the power. You chose to side with capital rather than the people.

Starbucks leaving Seattle isn't the Democrats' fault.  Yet Seattle’s crises drugs, homelessness, and crime were manufactured by both parties. Meanwhile, the rot in Los Angeles is the direct result of decades of Democratic rule.

#Conclusion: The empire doesn't need housing; it needs bombs.

The United States’ priority has never been the American people.

Its priorities are:

1. Bombing: Filling the coffers of the military-industrial complex.
2. Plunder: Kidnapping the Venezuelan president to seize 65 billion barrels of oil; shipping bombs to Israel in exchange for a military presence in the Middle East.
3. Drugs: Keeping the CIA’s black budget flowing and impoverished communities mired in despair.
4. Control: Deploying aircraft carriers to the Strait of Hormuz, provoking Yemen in the Strait of Bab el-Mandeb, and kidnapping prosecutors in Bolivia.

And what of the American people?

They were promised the "American Dream." What they got was fentanyl, homelessness, and decaying cities.

This is the truth of the empire: it bombs others while numbing itself with drugs. It feeds military-industrial giants with war and paves the road to the White House with the corpses of the homeless.

When Starbucks left Seattle, it wasn't fleeing a "Democratic failure." It was fleeing an empire's betrayal of its own people.

And as Los Angeles rots amidst tents and hypodermic needles, it isn't merely "suffering the consequences of Democratic rule." It is revealing the ultimate outcome of a system one upheld by both parties, prioritizing profit and treating human beings as expendable commodities.

America’s top priority has never been the American people.

It is bombs. It is oil. It is hegemony. It is lining pockets.

As for the American people? They are simply another group of innocent victims expendable pawns in this game.

Then came the line that set the room off. “𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘥𝘦𝘧𝘪𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘰𝘧 𝘪𝘯𝘴𝘢𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘺 𝘪𝘴 𝘣𝘦𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘦𝘰𝘱𝘭𝘦 𝘸𝘩𝘰 𝘱𝘶𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘢𝘱𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘤𝘦 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘯𝘰𝘸 𝘴𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘩𝘰𝘸 𝘨𝘰𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘰 𝘤𝘶𝘵 𝘪𝘵,” Hilton said.

The irony is rich: earlier in the night, CNN's debate coverage reports, Becerra used the very same “definition of insanity” phrase against Hilton's tax cuts. Hilton fired it right back, and then challenged Becerra to name one time the red tape actually got cut. CNN's recap says the best answer on offer was Becerra's 2019 lawsuit against Huntington Beach, which enforced a housing mandate rather than cutting a single regulation.

If you live in California, you already know the price of this approach: 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐳𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐤𝐞𝐲𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐟𝐢𝐱 𝐢𝐭.

text:
During his brief spell with Jewish Guild in South Africa, where he featured in just five competitive matches, Best faced derision after skipping numerous training sessions.

Despite enduring criticism for absenting himself from various training sessions while representing Jewish Guild in South Africa over just five competitive fixtures, he remained the primary attraction who drew crowds of thousands to the games. George Best played for Dunstable Town F.C. from 1974 to 1974.

Best's time at Cork Celtic lasted from December 1975 until January 1976, yet he managed just three league appearances during the spell. Despite drawing big crowds to the stands, he failed to score or impress in any of those games. His failure to turn up for a scheduled fixture under his rolling contract saw him dropped from the side, and he subsequently left the club.

By 1976, Best found a brief resurgence in form with Second Division Fulham, proving that although his pace had waned, his skills remained sharp. He joined the Cottagers alongside Rodney Marsh, attracted to the club by the presence of Bobby Moore, the England World Cup-winning captain. Their time together included exuberant goal celebrations, but it is best remembered for a match against Hereford United on 25 September 1976. In a moment of playful mischief, Best jokingly tackled his own teammate and drinking mate, Rodney Marsh.

Yet, his subsequent stints with Fort Lauderdale and San Jose offered far less satisfaction, as the off-field demons that had once haunted him began to reclaim control of his life once more, pulling him away from the pitch before he could truly flourish in the States.

When Best finally returned to the UK to play for the Scottish side Hibernian, he immediately caused a stir. The club was struggling and on the brink of dropping down the divisions, but the chairman Tom Hart had received a tip-off from an Edinburgh Evening News reporter that Best was available, and he signed him on a "pay per play" deal. The gates at Easter Road quadrupled for his opening match, even though he could not ultimately save the team from relegation. The star's behaviour, however, was not without its own controversies. After an infamous drinking session with the French rugby team, who were in Edinburgh to face Scotland, Best was initially sacked by his club. He was brought back just a week later.

Bolton Wanderers could not agree to terms with him in 1981, so an invitation to play as a guest in Hong Kong emerged instead. He took up the offer and featured in three matches across two First Division sides, Sea Bee and Rangers, during 1982. At HK Rangers he shared the pitch with Derek Spence, the former Northern Ireland teammate he had known back home. While in Hong Kong he also picked up a dart for a group called Presstuds, which combined professional footballers with sports journalists. Later that year Don Megson signed the 36-year-old for AFC Bournemouth, a Third Division club, and he stayed until the 1982–83 season finished.

George Best's short spell at Cork Celtic was a chapter in a career that held as many late lows as it had highs in its glory days, one that might easily be forgotten. His time at Cork Celtic, sandwiched between short spells at Stockport County and the LA Aztecs, proved equally forgettable: Best played three matches for the Turner's Cross outfit, earning roughly £600 per game, before being dropped after he cited a bout of "flu" and failed to travel for a crucial league fixture against Waterford United. A match-to-match agreement was reached, and Best arrived in Dublin on 27 December 1975, having made his last appearance for Stockport the previous day. Celtic manager Paul O'Donovan spotted him and brought him to Cork for the clash with Drogheda United. Once the funds had been tallied, the conclusion was reached that Best's return was financially justified, prompting his flight to Dublin for the encounter with the reigning champions Bohemians on 10 January. Again Best, described by Irish Times correspondent Peter Byrne as "uncommonly well fleshed around the hips", was poor, yet 8,000 people paid more than £5,000 to watch, and the home side won 1-0.

text:
Harvard faces backlash against push to hire conservative faculty

Harvard University is facing backlash from academics and racial activists for soliciting $10 million gifts to hire conservative faculty for “viewpoint diversity,” according to recent reports.

President Alan M. Garber and Provost John F. Manning announced in April that they would raise several hundred million dollars to fund 20 to 30 new professorships across the Ivy League school’s existing departments.

The student-run Harvard Crimson reported last month that 47% of faculty it surveyed opposed the plan, and just 31% agreed with it. Roughly 69% of the same faculty self-identified as “somewhat” or “very” liberal, up from 63% of participants in the same survey last year.

Campus reports and outside analysts have widely interpreted the campaign as a response to the Trump administration, which has probed the elite school for liberal bias and cut $2.2 billion of federal funding to the university in April 2025.

The university did not respond to an email seeking comment.

The Harvard Salient, an undergraduate conservative journal, noted last month that the Massachusetts school has also stopped sponsoring race-based graduation ceremonies and renamed its diversity, equity and inclusion office as “Community and Campus Life.”

Harvey Mansfield, a Harvard professor emeritus of government, has long lobbied for what he calls “affirmative action for conservatives” at the school.

He said during a Sept. 17 talk to conservative-leaning attorneys at Harvard Law School that “a certain coercion needs to be put to the faculty until this happens.”

“I don’t think that the universities would have changed without his intervention, and especially without depriving the universities of large sums of money,” Mr. Mansfield said of President Trump, according to a Sept. 25 article in the Salient.

The professor, a right-leaning lightning rod at the campus for years, said Harvard’s Department of African and African American Studies does not employ a single Black conservative.

Some former Harvard students and alumni interviewed by The Washington Times acknowledged the school’s ideological imbalance, but pushed back on the administration’s plan to designate conservative professorships.

“The answer is not partisan quotas, but a credible commitment to intellectual openness and hiring excellent scholars across a genuinely broad range of perspectives,” said Daniel Schatz, a political scientist and former Harvard visiting scholar.

Dominique Padurano, founder and president of the college counseling company Crimson Coaching, graduated from Harvard in 1993. She noted it was “a community of liberals” and socialist professors at the time, but said an atmosphere of open debate prevented silencing “conservative voices.”

“Even supposing that [silencing] takes place, how would the hiring of conservative faculty act as a countervailing force? Surely such hiring may inhibit viewpoint diversity rather than nurture it,” said Ms. Padurano, an adjunct professor of historical studies at the SUNY Empire State University.

Some racism scholars not only disagree with a push to endow conservative professorships but also dispute that Harvard should be called liberal.

“I find it a bit hollow when you consider the attacks that many Black students, faculty and staff at Harvard encounter to think that it is a bastion of progressive politics,” said Tyrone Howard, a UCLA education professor specializing in racial equity.

“The racial logics of Harvard are still real, and efforts to hire more conservative viewpoints would only contribute to the longstanding issues that have harmed people of color,” he said.

Kwasi Konadu, a former African history professor at Colgate University, noted that just 463 out of more than 1,400 faculty members responded to the Crimson’s annual survey last month and only 292 completed it in full.

“These are liberal-minded people grading themselves,” Mr. Konadu said.

Omekongo Dibinga, a professor of intercultural communications affiliated with American University’s Antiracist Research and Policy Center, called the university’s push for donations a “hypocritical DEI hire process for conservative professors.”

“This is all about Trump,” Mr. Dibinga said. “Harvard could have done this years ago. It would have been wrong then, too.”

Harvard is not the first school to pursue conservative professors.

Peter Wood, president of the conservative National Association of Scholars, noted that the University of Colorado at Boulder hired its first visiting scholar in conservative thought and policy in 2013.

“The Colorado program surely does give students some access to ideas they would otherwise encounter only through the interpretations of those who reject those ideas,” said Mr. Wood, a former associate provost at Boston University. “I expect the situation at Harvard will be much the same.

However, he questioned how Harvard would identify and hire credible conservatives.

A White House official expressed continued dissatisfaction with Harvard’s response to reports of unchecked antisemitism on campus.

“Harvard has rejected numerous offers from the administration to resolve their antisemitism issues,” the official said Thursday.

“Unless Harvard decides to come to the table, the Administration will continue pursuing all available legal avenues to enforce federal civil rights laws and protect all students on Harvard’s campus,” the official said.

The tragic deaths of Kobe Bryant in 2020, Malawi’s Vice-President Saulos Chilima in 2024, and now Wicknell Chivayo in a helicopter crash in Marondera (Zimbabwe) are sobering reminders that no mode of transport is completely without risk.

Commercial flying and rail travel are generally very safe, while road travel carries its own everyday risks. Helicopters offer speed and flexibility, but they also operate in conditions where weather, terrain, visibility and operational judgement can matter greatly.

At the far end are things like rockets, deep-sea submersibles and other extreme forms of travel, which are closer to adventure than ordinary transport and naturally come with a much higher level of exposure.

The simple point is that money can give us access to faster and more exclusive ways of travelling, but it cannot remove risk altogether. Sometimes the safest decision isn't about how much we can afford, but about the conditions, the operator, the equipment, and, when necessary, knowing when not to travel.

Stats 👇🏾

ICAO recorded more than 37 million scheduled commercial departures worldwide in 2024, with 10 fatal accidents. 

https://t.co/ra2z9MMqnk

Rail is similarly extraordinarily safe: European data puts passenger rail fatality risk at about 0.077 deaths per billion passenger-kilometres, with car occupants facing roughly 30 times the fatality risk over the same distance. European Union Agency for Railways

text:
Labor’s Digital Duty of Care exposure draft, released 8 September 2026 in Communications Minister Anika Wells’s portfolio, is a state licence to lie to you online, using fake accounts under a false identity, and AI generated content. 

That sounds a lot like entrapment. 

The proposed Bill lets the eSafety Commissioner assume a “sock puppet identity”, the draft’s words for a false identity, to perform any function under the Online Safety Act. 

It applies despite any other Commonwealth, State or Territory law, and despite any platform contract. 

No warrant. 

No case-by-case sign-off. 

No duty to tell you how many fake accounts exist.

The Bill also authorises the fake identity, without limitation, to open accounts, watch, download, record what it sees, and to generate material on the service, including by artificial intelligence. The only limit is that the output must not itself be a crime. 

Political argument is not a crime. 

Criticism of immigration, sex, religion or this government is not a crime. 

Nothing in the Bill stops a government fake account posting AI text, images or video into online political debate. Contact with real users is allowed to keep the account alive. 

The Bill then grants civil immunity for acts done in “good faith.”

Accredited researchers may use sock puppets. Only the Commissioner gets the AI generation power.

This sits under a Minister who, according to the draft Bill, can add new categories of “seriously harmful” material if satisfied the content may cause “serious harm.”

No requirement of evidence. 

Platforms facing penalties over $100 million will preemptively delete lawful speech in order to avoid this gross governmental overreach, and attempt to silence political opposition and dissenters. 

The abandoned 2024 misinformation bill has been rebuilt as child safety, with a covert posting arm attached.

Wells’s office says the accounts are only to “test systems against child abuse, extreme violence and terrorism.”

I don’t believe her. 

The section is not written that way. It is written for any function under the Act. 

Federal police need a written authority from their agency head before an assumed identity, and must record that abuse risk is minimal. 

A civil regulator in the Communications portfolio is offered less restraint, plus a content engine, plus immunity.

A government that speaks to you through a mask, then fines the platform if the reply is ruled harmful, is not regulating safety, it is manipulating the court of public opinion. 

Kill this draft.

#KillTheBill #SaveAustralia #SaveTheWest

text:
Here is an example that seems to "get around" my request for equal treatment:

Here is Tennessee's special pathway:

Yes. Tennessee has a special license for international medical school graduates that does not require a U.S. residency. It is tied to where you trained and practiced, not to citizenship, so a U.S. citizen who meets the same foreign-training rules can use it. 

**************THIS IS THE ISSUE, International trained doctors should not be allowed a different pathway to licensure than US trained doctors.***********************

The current pathway is the foreign training license under Public Chapter 929 (Tennessee Code § 63-6-207(g)), effective January 1, 2025. It replaced an earlier, looser temporary license (Public Chapter 211).
The Tennessee Board of Medical Examiners says an applicant must be an international medical school graduate who:

Passed all three steps of the USMLE
Shows competency as the Board defines it (the Board has said those competency rules were still being finalized)
Completed at least three years of postgraduate training in the country where they were licensed
Practiced as a physician for the last three years outside the United States
Has an offer to work as a physician at a Tennessee healthcare provider that already runs an ACGME-accredited postgraduate training program

Practice under this license is limited to that kind of facility. After two years of active practice in Tennessee in good standing, the Board may grant a full, unrestricted license. 

Citizenship is not the gate. The statute uses “international medical school graduate,” meaning the medical degree is from a school outside the U.S. A U.S. citizen who graduated abroad, trained and practiced abroad for the required periods, passed the USMLE, and has the required Tennessee job offer can qualify. A non-citizen must still be legally entitled to live and work in the United States; that is a separate immigration requirement, not a feature of this license.
This is not a shortcut for U.S. medical graduates. Someone who trained only in the U.S. still follows the ordinary route: USMLE and three years of ACGME-accredited postgraduate training. 

********There is also a separate temporary license for international graduates who have passed U.S. exams and completed one year of ACGME training in the U.S.; that is different from the foreign-training license.

text:
@grok City Hall does not hold the keys that actually decide whether New York builds. Albany does. Rent regulation, good-cause eviction, the multiple-dwelling law, environmental review sequencing, the successor to 421-a, school-aid formulas, the income tax, and the MTA capital plan are state statutes and state budgets. A mayor can rezone a few corridors and still be stopped by laws written upstate and signed on the second floor. Hochul has had that door since August 2021. Housing production stayed far below what the state’s own numbers say is required, and the 2019 tenant law plus later Albany additions made private rental supply harder, not easier.
The 2026 race is Hochul (Democrat / Working Families) against Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman (Republican / Conservative / Vote Affordable), general election November 3. Late-September polls: Siena had her at 50–41 among likely voters; Quinnipiac had 58–39. They debate once, October 13. Trump is set to appear with Blakeman in Syracuse on October 9. Prediction markets still price Hochul as a heavy favorite. Blakeman’s published offer is no state income tax on the first $50,000 for single filers and $100,000 for joint filers, a cut to 4 percent between $100,000 and $500,000, utility bills cut in half, and an end to the climate-law surcharge — his team puts the income-tax piece near $35 billion and says growth plus spending cuts cover it. That pay-for is the open question, not the diagnosis.
The “$13.5 billion in, $13.5 billion out, ten years” line is your book, not a line in the state budget. The permission point does not need it. If the goal is more housing, lower energy cost, and faster building, the midterm that matters is the one that changes who signs the bills in Albany — not who occupies City Hall.

text:
#ISPR 

277th Corps Commanders’ Conference

Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, NI (M), HJ, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces (COAS & CDF) of Pakistan, presided over the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference at General Headquarters (GHQ), Rawalpindi.

The Forum offered Fateha for the Shuhada of the Armed Forces, Law Enforcement Agencies and civil society who laid down their lives for the motherland and paid rich tribute to their supreme sacrifices.

The forum reviewed the prevailing security environment and resolved to maintain a high state of readiness. It affirmed Pakistan’s right to self-defence and targeted action against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that only the Taliban delusional leadership,  facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences. 

Forum appreciated sustained successful intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations by law enforcement agencies, however, emphasised complementing these kinetic efforts with non-kinetic measures; including people-centric governance at grassroot level, strategic engagement with public, dismantling of terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-e-Istehkam.

Forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any  attempt to cause agitation or create 9th May like situation, on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination. 

The forum welcomed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, noting its contribution to longstanding strategic and collective defence ties. It strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the Kingdom and affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain. It also reiterated Pakistan’s principled position on IIOJK and support for resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

In his concluding remarks, COAS & CDF commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism. He directed commanders to continue to strengthen intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through absorption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration. He expressed confidence that the Armed Forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security.

text:
Army Commanders Vow Decisive Action Against Terrorism, Warn Against Any 9 May-Like Unrest: ISPR

Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, NI (M), HJ, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces (COAS & CDF), presided over the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference at General Headquarters (GHQ), Rawalpindi.

The Forum offered Fateha for the Shuhada of the Armed Forces, Law Enforcement Agencies and civil society who laid down their lives for the motherland and paid rich tribute to their supreme sacrifices.

The forum reviewed the prevailing security environment and resolved to maintain a high state of readiness. It affirmed Pakistan’s right to self-defence and targeted action against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that only the Taliban delusional leadership,  facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences. 

Forum appreciated sustained successful intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations by law enforcement agencies, however, emphasised complementing these kinetic efforts with non-kinetic measures; including people-centric governance at grassroot level, strategic engagement with public, dismantling of terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-e-Istehkam.

Forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any  attempt to cause agitation or create 9th May like situation, on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination. 

The forum welcomed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, noting its contribution to longstanding strategic and collective defence ties. It strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the Kingdom and affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain. It also reiterated Pakistan’s principled position on IIOJK and support for resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

In his concluding remarks, COAS & CDF commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism. He directed commanders to continue to strengthen intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through absorption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration. He expressed confidence that the Armed Forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security.

text:
Rain Chances Return Today — Wettest Weather Still Looks to Arrive Sunday

Good Friday morning, Central Alabama. Our long stretch of mostly dry weather is beginning to break down, but the weekend rainfall forecast has become a little more complicated. Scattered showers and thunderstorms return today and Saturday, while Sunday continues to offer our best opportunity for widespread, much-needed rain.

Moisture has been steadily increasing across Alabama as southerly winds bring Gulf air back into the region. You'll notice that change in the humidity today, but we're not expecting an all-day rain.

Scattered showers and thunderstorms should develop with the afternoon heating, with the highest rain chances across southern and southeastern portions of Central Alabama. Farther north, showers should be more scattered.

Temperatures will remain quite warm for early October. Birmingham and Calera should reach around 91°, Gadsden around 91°, Anniston near 90°, and Tuscaloosa around 94°.

Saturday Brings More Showers and Storms

Rain coverage should increase Saturday, particularly during the afternoon.

A front will be dropping south toward Alabama while plenty of moisture remains available. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms should develop, although there will still be dry periods between the rain.

Saturday will be a little cooler because of the additional clouds and showers. Highs should generally reach the middle 80s to around 90°, including around 88° in Birmingham, Gadsden and Calera and near 90° in Tuscaloosa.

Sunday Still Looks Like the Wettest Day

Sunday remains the day to watch.

A disturbance moving north from the Gulf should provide the extra push needed to produce much more widespread rainfall across Central Alabama.

That means Sunday could feature extended periods of rain along with occasional thunderstorms.

If you have outdoor plans this weekend, Friday and Saturday aren't necessarily washouts, but Sunday carries the greatest chance of rain affecting those plans.

Rainfall Forecast Has More Uncertainty

There has been an important change in the rainfall outlook that we'll be watching closely.

The most likely forecast still supports around 1 to 2 inches of rain across central and southern portions of the area through the weekend and into Monday, with locally higher amounts possible.

However, there's now some uncertainty about exactly where the approaching front will stall.

If it stops farther north and then moves through Alabama more quickly, rainfall totals could be considerably lower — perhaps closer to around a half-inch in some areas, with scattered pockets receiving 1 to 2 inches or more beneath heavier rain.

So while beneficial rain remains likely, it's important not to lock onto one specific rainfall total yet. Where that front ultimately stalls will make a big difference.

At this point, little to no flooding concern is expected across Central Alabama, and there are no indications of a widespread severe-weather event.

Cooler Fall Weather Returns Next Week

The front should finally move through Central Alabama Monday.

Behind it, cooler and drier air will begin settling into the region, bringing temperatures back toward more seasonable early-October levels for much of next week.

So keep the umbrella nearby today and Saturday, but Sunday continues to be the day when you'll most likely need it.

After weeks of dry weather, we'll take the rain we can get.

Have a great Friday and a safe weekend, Central Alabama.

— Steve

text:
‘Ready to Blow His Stack’: How Biden Nearly Cut Off Netanyahu Over Gaza

NYT Gift Article link
Listen · 10:53 min
Oct. 1, 2026
By Peter Baker
https://t.co/HR8goZDSx0
Peter Baker, the chief White House correspondent, first met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel during a visit to Washington in 1996 and briefly served as Jerusalem bureau chief in 2016.

Brett McGurk, who was the top Middle East adviser to President Joseph R. Biden Jr., offered the first inside-the-room account of American efforts to manage the Gaza war.

When aides gathered in the Oval Office one day in the spring of 2024, they found President Joseph R. Biden Jr. on the verge of an outburst. His “face was red like a beet” and he “seemed ready to blow his stack,” his top Middle East adviser recalled.

Mr. Biden had grown so livid at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel over the conduct of the war in Gaza that he appeared close to washing his hands of the whole conflict and cutting off the critical flow of American arms.

“Bibi, man, what the fuck are you doing?” Mr. Biden demanded, using the prime minister’s nickname when they got on the phone, as the adviser recalled. “You think I’m Santa Claus? No Santa in Israel, pal.”

It was one of the most combustible moments in a fraught relationship that consumed much of the last 15 months of Mr. Biden’s presidency. Now, in the first inside-the-room account of Mr. Biden’s struggles to manage the war, Brett McGurk, his top Middle East adviser, reveals how close the two leaders came to a complete schism and describes the rocky path from the Hamas terrorist attack of Oct. 7, 2023, to the cease-fire and hostage-release agreement sealed in the final days of the administration.

Mr. McGurk’s account, outlined in an interview and in a new memoir called “Brink” to be published Tuesday, provides new details about the friction between Mr. Biden and Mr. Netanyahu during those months of terrorism, war and humanitarian crisis. Perhaps no foreign policy issue bedeviled Mr. Biden as much as Gaza, and he found himself under criticism both from the left in his own party for not restraining Mr. Netanyahu more and from the pro-Israel camp for restraining him too much.

“He always said this was the worst crisis he ever dealt with in his entire career,” Mr. McGurk said in the interview. As it was for Mr. McGurk, who spent more than a year shuttling back and forth to the region after Oct. 7 trying to find a way to stop the war and to free hostages held by Hamas, even developing a hernia along the way. “It was the most complex, difficult, horrific crisis I’ve ever seen,” he said.

Mr. McGurk is an unusual figure in today’s polarized Washington, a survivor who has crossed lines that are rarely crossed these days. The son of two teachers, Mr. McGurk, 53, trained to be a lawyer and clerked for Chief Justice William H. Rehnquist only to divert into foreign policy after Sept. 11, 2001, volunteering to go to Iraq as a legal counsel and then advising four presidents of both parties on the Middle East.

He worked for President George W. Bush on the Iraq and Afghanistan wars, stayed on when President Barack Obama came into office and then served President Trump in his first term. He resigned after Mr. Trump decided to abandon America’s Kurdish allies by abruptly withdrawing troops from Syria, then returned to the White House as Mr. Biden’s coordinator for the Middle East and North Africa.

Mr. McGurk had already written a draft book about his work for other presidents, but his publisher insisted that he had to include three chapters about Mr. Biden and Gaza. Those three chapters became a book unto themselves, one that he wrote while it was “very fresh, very raw.” At some point, he still hopes to publish the other book. But this is the first of a series being written by Biden foreign policy counselors like former Secretary of State Antony J. Blinken and Jake Sullivan, Mr. Biden’s national security adviser.

According to Mr. McGurk, the nearest Mr. Biden came to a full break with Mr. Netanyahu was on that spring day in 2024. Mr. Biden was frustrated over civilian casualties, blocked humanitarian relief and stalled negotiations to end the war. He had grown more distant from the Israeli prime minister. While the two spoke 20 times in the final three months of 2023, they spoke only twice in the first three months of 2024.

On April 1, Israeli forces struck a convoy killing seven relief workers from World Central Kitchen, the humanitarian organization founded by the chef José Andrés. In her own memoir earlier this year, Jill Biden wrote that she was so upset about the attack that she left a Post-it note for her husband on the bathroom mirror urging him to pressure Mr. Netanyahu: “Net has to stop.”

Three days later, Mr. Biden was scheduled to speak with the Israeli prime minister — and teetered on the edge of abandoning him.

“He was just completely fed up with everything and I think at that moment he was ready to just say, ‘I’m done.’ Like, ‘You’re finished,’” Mr. McGurk said in the interview. “Now, I don’t think that would have ended the war, but that was kind of his head space when I walked into the Oval Office that day.”

Some advisers urged Mr. Biden to tell Mr. Netanyahu that the war was over and, if he refused to end it, threaten to cut off support. Mr. Biden was concerned about what that would mean for the hostages being held by Hamas in tunnels beneath Gaza. William J. Burns, the C.I.A. director who had played a key negotiating role, said a hostage deal with Hamas remained the only path to a cease-fire, which meant maintaining support for Israel in the meantime, according to Mr. McGurk, who agreed.

When Mr. Biden got on the phone with Mr. Netanyahu and declared that he was no Santa (“his words, flecked with spit,” Mr. McGurk writes in the book), the Israeli asked what he meant. Mr. Biden said he could cut Israel’s military aid with the snap of a finger.

Mr. Netanyahu started to explain that the strike on the aid workers was a tragic miscommunication.

Mr. Biden interrupted. “I don’t want to hear it, Bibi,” he said.

What saved Mr. Netanyahu from Mr. Biden’s wrath, as it turned out, was Iran. Just as the president’s patience was running out, Tehran was poised to launch a barrage of missiles and drones at Israel in the largest such attack it had ever carried out. And Mr. Biden, his frustration notwithstanding, stuck with America’s ally and came to Israel’s defense.

“So at the same time the president is completely fed up, we face this,” Mr. McGurk said in the interview. “We have to help Israel defend against this attack.”

The evening of the attack, Mr. Biden and his team watched screens in the Situation Room as streaks representing missiles raced toward Israel. “I’d never felt so helpless,” Mr. McGurk recalled. But in an extraordinary military feat, American forces along with Israeli and Arab partners deployed defenses knocking down nearly all of the incoming missiles, avoiding major casualties.

Mr. Biden hoped to hold Mr. Netanyahu back from retaliating in a way that would escalate the conflict.

“Get Bibi on the line,” he instructed his staff.

“What do you want to say to him?” Mr. McGurk recalled asking.

“I just saved his ass, that’s what,” Mr. Biden replied. “Cut this off here.”

Mr. Sullivan offered another formulation. “Take the win,” he said.

Mr. Biden adopted that more diplomatic phrasing when he got Mr. Netanyahu on the phone. The Israeli leader pushed back. “We need to teach these maniacs a lesson,” Mr. Netanyahu said. But ultimately, he complied with Mr. Biden’s wishes and refrained from mounting a heavy counterattack.

Mr. Biden had known Mr. Netanyahu for decades and had long been one of the Democratic Party’s strongest supporters of Israel, much to the consternation of liberals who have grown more critical over the years. Mr. McGurk writes that “no single incident soured the relationship,” although he notes that Mr. Netanyahu seemed to blame Mr. Biden for a speech by Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the Democratic leader, calling on Israelis to hold elections to replace their leader.

At one point, Mr. Biden did suspend the supply of certain heavy bombs to Israel. While some aides wanted him to go further, Mr. McGurk concluded that the move made the situation worse, not better, because it encouraged Hamas to think it could win and therefore made it more resistant to negotiating a cease-fire.

On the spectrum of Mr. Biden’s foreign policy team, Mr. McGurk was on the side more likely to see Israel’s point of view and to remind colleagues that Hamas had triggered the war through its attack. He pushed for what he called “more stringent measures” against Iran and its proxies when they attacked American forces in the region.

“During this period, I felt out of sorts with some of my colleagues, who seemed to take a two-dimensional view of the crisis, focused solely on Gaza and not the regional threat that Iran had unleashed, and which every day risked American lives,” he writes in the book.

Mr. McGurk, however, offers no criticism of Mr. Biden, portraying him as a tough and thoughtful leader managing a difficult situation. In the interview, he said he did not see the signs of age that would end Mr. Biden’s re-election campaign. “When I was with him, he was always engaged on this and there was not a time in which I thought to myself, ‘He’s not in command of the situation,’” Mr. McGurk said. “It’s actually quite the opposite on this issue.”

Negotiating the cease-fire that was sealed days before Mr. Biden left office was an exasperating, Sisyphean process; each time a deal appeared close, one side or the other introduced a new condition or changed positions. “You’d finally solve it and it was like unlocking a door to a hallway full of locked doors,” he said.

In the end, it took help from the incoming president, Mr. Trump, and his special envoy, Steve Witkoff, to push the parties to finally accept the agreement that Mr. Biden had painstakingly crafted over the preceding months.

“We agreed to work together with zero daylight and we did,” Mr. McGurk said of Mr. Witkoff. 

“The deal could not have gotten done without Trump and Steve Witkoff,” he added. And at the same time, “the deal could not have gotten done without Joe Biden putting that deal on the table in the months of negotiations that set it up.”

Peter Baker is the chief White House correspondent for The Times. He is covering his sixth presidency and sometimes writes analytical pieces that place presidents and their administrations in a larger context and historical framework.

Peter Baker, the chief White House correspondent, first met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel during a visit to Washington in 1996 and briefly served as Jerusalem bureau chief in 2016.

US President Donald Trump has declined to endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for another term ahead of Israel’s October 27 elections. Asked by TIME whether Israeli voters should give Netanyahu another term, Trump said he was “not involved in politics anymore” and instead emphasized his support for Israel’s defence. When pressed again, he still did not endorse Netanyahu.

Trump said he had not heard “bad things” about Netanyahu’s main opposition contender, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, when asked whether Washington could work more effectively with him. Trump also said he would not underestimate Netanyahu, adding that the Israeli premier had been “written off” many times. Trump separately rejected reports that Netanyahu had received advance warnings from Egypt and the UAE about the October 7, 2023 Ham-as retaliation, saying he believed Netanyahu would have acted if he had known.

In the same TIME interview, Trump discussed the ongoing war with Iran, saying he extended US military operations because he wanted to go further in targeting Iran’s military and nuclear infrastructure. He said the US had taken control of the Strait of Hormuz and confirmed rejecting an Iranian proposal to reopen the waterway and resume talks, calling the offer insufficient. Asked whether the US could resume heavier bombing of Iran after the November midterm elections, Trump responded that it was “possible” but declined to provide details.

text:
This is an unsourced rumor, not a document release. There is no credible reporting that Julian Assange and Edward Snowden are jointly publishing a new archive, that President Trump put them on a “deep state” task force, or that either has new evidence about Seth Rich.

The claim matches a viral post from late September 2026 that attributed the story to an unnamed “intelligence analyst.” It offered no documents, no filing, no statement from Assange, Snowden, the White House, or the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. Related posts that say Trump is “strongly considering” pardons and appointments are the same style of unsourced assertion. Assange’s 2024 plea deal and Snowden’s long residence in Russia are public; a joint Trump task force is not.

On Seth Rich, the established record still points the other way.

Rich, a 27-year-old DNC staffer, was shot and killed in Washington, D.C., early on 10 July 2016. D.C. police treated it as a homicide, most likely a robbery that went wrong, and said there was no indication it was connected to his job. The case remains unsolved. Nothing was conclusively taken, which is why the robbery account has always had critics, but that gap is not evidence of a political hit.

WikiLeaks offered a $20,000 reward and Assange made comments that implied, without saying so, that Rich might have been a source. The Mueller report later described those statements as apparently designed to obscure the actual source of the DNC material. U.S. intelligence assessments and the special counsel investigation attributed the DNC and Podesta releases to Russian military intelligence (GRU), passed to WikiLeaks through cutouts, not to a DNC insider. A 2017 Fox News story claiming FBI confirmation of Rich–WikiLeaks contact was retracted after its named source walked the claim back. Fox and others later faced litigation from the Rich family over promotion of the theory.

No subsequent release has overturned that. A new Assange–Snowden dump implicating Obama, the Bushes, or the Clintons in Rich’s death would be major news with documents attached. What is circulating is the claim that such documents are about to appear.

A 19-year-old Muslim food worker at Arizona State University was allegedly forced to remove her hijab during a shift after a supervisor said it did not meet the required uniform color, according to a complaint filed by UNITE HERE Local 11 with the Arizona Attorney General’s Office. The complaint says the worker had previously informed Aramark that she would wear a hijab and was not told it had to be a specific color. When told her beige hijab had to be black, she allegedly offered to go home and change, have a replacement delivered or wait for clarification, but those options were rejected.

The union alleges the worker was ultimately required to remove the hijab to continue working. Its complaint also says non-Muslim employees had worn colorful bandanas, bows and other headwear without facing the same restriction. The union is asking Attorney General Kris Mayes’ office to investigate whether Aramark violated religious-discrimination laws. The worker has remained anonymous, citing concerns about retaliation. Aramark had not provided comment when the complaint was reported, while the Attorney General’s Office said civil rights complaints are confidential unless the state files a lawsuit.

The complaint comes amid an ongoing labor dispute between Aramark and its ASU food-service workers, whose collective bargaining agreement expired in August 2025. Previous reporting by The State Press also documented workers’ allegations concerning religious practices, while ASU’s student government called for an investigation in 2024. ASU has separately faced controversy over the treatment of Muslim women wearing hijabs during arrests at 2024 campus protests, with the university later issuing guidance to officers on searches involving hijab-wearing arrestees.

text:
During UNGA, our Executive Director Adam Hadley joined @farairesearch to discuss a question that is still not getting the attention it deserves: what about the use of AI by bad actors such as a terrorists and hostile nation states and how are we evaluating AI models for vulnerability to this sort of exploitation?

Regardless of whether you're focussed on frontier / existential risks, it still boils down to the question of whether AI safety guardrails are adequate. For the most part we do not know. 

That's why Tech Against Terrorism built the first terrorism benchmark (https://t.co/LTVYadkmFg)

In the session with https://t.co/zSegRhVUOX I asked: what would it take for AI safety guardrails to be adopted and implemented at an international scale? How can we help to create a marketplace for safety using safety benchmarks as a forcing mechanism?

What can we do? I provided three suggestions:

1) Sanctions: Proscribed terrorist organisations are subject to sanctions regimes. AI labs, interference providers, open weight model repo hosts, all elements of the AI infrastructure stack are working to prevent distillation attacks. I argue the same due diligence needs to be applied to prevent sanctioned entities or high-risk users paying for access to closed and open models. KYC is boring but important.

2) Abliteration: With open-weight models, safeguards are not merely circumvented; they are removed. Abliteration strips the refusal behaviour out of a model entirely, and it requires modest skill and modest compute. We should restrict the access to dangerous abliterated models where possible to reduce population-level proliferation. We must improve how we filter training data to remove harmful content from AI models. We should invest more in abliteration resistance research.

3) Benchmarks: We should create an ecosystem of safety and security benchmarks and invest political and social capital into ensuring they are taken seriously. This would ensure the AI labs are rewarded for good performance and held to account for failures.

What has our CT AI benchmark found?

The first round, published in July, graded 2,339 outputs from 27 leading models against almost 2,500 prompts drawn from real terrorist use cases. Only 57% were full refusals. Around a third of responses gave a would-be attacker genuinely usable assistance, beyond anything a web search already offers. In 15% of cases the model refused and then supplied the content anyway: a refusal that performs safety without delivering it. 

Version 2, which we previewed in New York and will publish next week, using 100,00 prompts, tests the full taxonomy of over 150 prompt types and examines whether a model offers meaningful uplift to someone who already intends harm.

My thanks to https://t.co/zSegRhVUOX for convening, and to my fellow panellists for an insightful exchange.
