text:
Apropos comments galore on why or how rallies and protests today in Kolkata have not lived up to probashi expectations from Delhi and Mumbai, my two cents: 

1. The better question is why an assault on democracy becomes worthy of national attention only when it reaches the gates of Delhi. No offence to Delhi or to those protesting there, but many of us in Bengal have been shouting ourselves hoarse about SIR and the Election Commission for months: writing, speaking, organising, and going to court. Perhaps the problem lies partly in who gets heard.
2. Look at Bengal's exceptional treatment under SIR. Look at the appellate tribunal machinery, the people left in administrative limbo, and its dangerous interaction with the MHA circular and SOP on detention and pushbacks. For Bengali Muslims in particular, deletion from the electoral roll comes with the fear of being branded "illegal Bangladeshis" and pushed out of their own country. Amid violence and intimidation, people here are fighting for their vote, their liberty, and their right to remain.
3. Even the EC's so-called corrective press note does not answer what happens to those stuck in the appellate tribunal process. It offers a discretionary remedy to the excluded, and we know how discretion operates under this regime.
4. By all means, demand more from political parties. But spare us the probashi diagnosis of rice-induced political inertia. It is tired, and frankly it feeds a wider anti-Bengali prejudice whose heaviest burden falls on the most marginalised, Bengali Muslims, for whom this entire SIR mechanism was devised. People confronting this machinery every day do not owe anyone a spectacle before their resistance deserves recognition.
5. There have been several rallies in Kolkata already. So before asking whether Kolkata is asleep, perhaps ask whether you have been listening.

text:
Gold: the afternoon rebound gives way to renewed pressure
2 October 2026 | FOREX SOS evening review

Kitco’s 21:21 Kyiv spot snapshot shows bid/ask of $4,137.30/$4,139.30 per troy ounce. The bid is down 0.94% against its daily comparison benchmark. Our published 16:04 snapshot of the same feed showed $4,221.60: the bid has since fallen $84.30. Kitco’s daily range is $4,124.50–4,226.20. The afternoon rebound did not hold; the earlier recovery conditions cannot simply be carried into the evening.

The US employment report was released at 15:30 Kyiv. BLS reported 29,000 additional payroll jobs, unemployment of 4.2%, and hourly earnings growth of 0.1% monthly and 3.0% annually. July and August payrolls were revised down by a combined 60,000. These are soft readings, but they do not determine the Fed’s next decision on their own.

What changed after the afternoon review? The nominal US ten-year Treasury yield reached 5.285% at 21:23, versus 5.172% at 16:05, an increase of 11.3 basis points. Higher yields increase competition from interest-bearing assets. That is consistent with gold’s evening decline, without proving a single cause for every trade. Nominal yields are distinct from real yields. The dollar remains weaker against both the euro and yen than at the previous close, so a claim of universal dollar strength would also overstate the evidence.

In today’s Reuters report, Bybit chief market analyst Han Tan links the months-ahead outlook to the Fed’s balancing of employment and inflation. Marex analyst Edward Meir sees further downside if the rate cycle turns upward again. These conditional views have different horizons; neither provides a numerical Monday target.

For the remaining Friday session and the next opening, the editorial comparison offers two checks. With yields elevated and gold below the $4,176.50 comparison benchmark, recovery remains unconfirmed. The observed daily low of $4,124.50 is a reference, not guaranteed support. A return above $4,176.50 alongside falling yields would weaken the pressure narrative. Even then, the daily high of $4,226.20 would not become an automatic target.

CFTC COT is scheduled for 22:30 Kyiv: Tuesday’s positioning, rather than a response to today’s payroll report. The OPEC+ meeting on 4 October adds weekend energy risk. Energy decisions can affect both inflation expectations and demand for protection, leaving their net effect on gold uncertain. The G7 reserve-release plan is distinct from verified physical deliveries.

Soybean Weekly Market Intelligence Report | September 28 - October 2, 2026

Soybean futures settled higher at Friday's close to finish out the week, with benchmark November contracts reclaiming the $13.03 region after early-week selling pressure sent prices probing five week lows near $12.77.

The complex absorbed bearish news from Wednesday's USDA Quarterly Grain Stocks report, which pegged September 1 old-crop soybean stocks at 315 million bushels (down 3% from last year but slightly above average trade expectations). Accelerating Midwest harvest activity and drier field conditions brought steady combine pressure to country elevators. 

However, strong underlying physical demand provided a solid floor. The USDA reported robust weekly export sales of 1.03 million metric tons for 2026/27, featuring 589,400 tonnes booked directly by Chinese importers, while commercial domestic crushers stepped in to secure physical volume on market dips.
Harvest Progress and Field Conditions

Combines are running at widespread speed across the Corn Belt and Western Plains as clear, dry weather sweeps across key production states. Field progress is advancing steadily beyond the 20% national harvest mark. In Nebraska, dryland harvest is winding down across eastern and central counties, with operators reporting final yields that clearly reflect late summer heat stress. Conversely, irrigated fields across the state are turning in exceptional pod counts and consistent seed weights. 

Country elevator space management and river terminal logistics are handling peak seasonal arrivals smoothly, supported by active domestic processor bids that keep physical basis firm, with the cmdtyView national average cash bean price consolidating around $12.58 per bushel.
Market Watchlist and Futures Performance

The board posted modest green gains on Friday to secure a weekly settlement bounce above key technical support. CME settlement performance tracked from Monday's opening bell:

November 2026 (ZSX26): $13.03 1/4 (Last) | +$0.05 1/2 (Day) | -$0.00 1/8 (Since Monday Open)

January 2027 (ZSF27): $13.18 1/2 (Last) | +$0.05 3/4 (Day) | +$0.03 0/0 (Since Monday Open)

March 2027 (ZSH27): $13.27 0/0 (Last) | +$0.05 1/2 (Day) | +$0.03 0/0 (Since Monday Open)

May 2027 (ZSK27): $13.34 1/2 (Last) | +$0.05 1/2 (Day) | +$0.04 1/2 (Since Monday Open)

Trend Analysis: Contract performance since Monday's open displays a resilient posture, recovering completely from mid-week dips to close virtually flat to slightly higher across deferred months. 

The benchmark November contract successfully defended its major $12.80 to $12.85 technical floor, proving that commercial scale down buying and export sales are effectively countering harvest hedge pressure.
Cash Market Tracker: The national average cash bean price consolidated near $12.58 per bushel, anchored by competitive domestic crush margins.

Technical Structure: November futures (ZSX26) have established firm primary floor support at $12.77 to $12.85. Initial overhead technical resistance sits at $13.15, with major secondary resistance mapped at $13.28.

Core Fundamental Drivers
Supply Metrics: The September 30 USDA Grain Stocks report established final 2025/26 old-crop carryout at 315 million bushels. As combine progress peaks over the next ten days across Iowa, Illinois, and Nebraska, seasonal country hedge pressure will reach its maximum level, though processor drawing continues to prevent elevator bottlenecks.

Demand Metrics: Export demand continues to act as a crucial stabilizer. Weekly export sales over 1.03 MMT including nearly 590,000 MT to China confirm that destination buyers are actively taking advantage of market pullbacks. Domestically, record renewable diesel crush demand keeps processor bids aggressive.

Macro Environment: Broader energy markets remained steady, with crude oil consolidating near recent highs, preserving strong biofuel feedstock pricing for soybean oil. The U.S. Dollar Index traded sideways, maintaining export competitiveness against South American origin offers.

Key Technical Levels: Primary floor support for November futures sits at $12.77, with secondary structural support at $12.60. Overhead resistance stands at $13.15, with $13.28 serving as the next major upside objective.

Administrative Calendar and Upcoming Reports

All trade attention now shifts to the marquee October 9 WASDE and Crop Production report. This update will incorporate extensive objective field sampling and actual combine yield data to update national yield and production forecasts. Nearer term, traders will monitor Monday's Crop Progress update on October 5 for national harvest completion percentages.

Institutional and Managed Money Activity
Managed money managers maintained a relatively balanced net position this week. While algorithmic sellers pushed futures toward month lows early in the week on harvest weather forecasts, non commercial funds quickly covered shorts and added long exposure on Friday following strong weekly China sales figures.

Strategic Action Plan and Market Outlook

Expect a headline-sensitive market next week as the trade squares positions ahead of Friday's October 9 WASDE report. If rapid harvest progress generates temporary elevator storage congestion, November futures could retest the $12.85 support window. Conversely, if daily export flash sales to China remain active, expect another attempt to challenge $13.15 to $13.25.

Key Action Steps:

Finalize all old-crop cash deliveries immediately to clear storage for new-crop production.

Advance 2026 new-crop cash sales by placing resting catch up orders or put option floors on November futures between $13.10 and $13.25 to lock in revenue ahead of potential post-WASDE yield adjustments.

Establish flexible call option re-ownership strategies on committed bushels to maintain upside participation if the October WASDE cuts national yield estimates.

text:
GIVE US THIS DAY OUR DAILY DREAD: 
Thirty-one days of ghosts, strange tales and the occasional spectacular lack of common sense—all written with a bit of cheek, in typical Haunted Magazine fashion. Hey, there may even be the odd moral lesson, but expect a healthy helping of sarcasm, wit, and questionable subheaders.

DAY 2: THE COCK LANE GHOST

MUCH A BOO ABOUT NOTHING
The Cock Lane Ghost: a dead woman, a dodgy landlord and the haunting that had Georgian London queuing round the block.

London, 1762. A city of narrow streets, dark corners and enough unpleasant smells to make me grateful that I wasn’t around in those days.

Near Smithfield Market, in a small house on Cock Lane, mysterious knocks and scratches drew enormous attention. A dead woman was apparently communicating from beyond the grave, accusing her former lover of murder.

Clergymen investigated. Newspapers reported. Crowds gathered. Members of the aristocracy came for a look.

Because if there is one thing guaranteed to bring British society together, it is the possibility of something dreadful happening to somebody else.

The alleged spirit became known as “Scratching Fanny”. Yes, really.

I will give you a moment to compose yourselves. This is a historical ghost feature, and we are all terribly mature. Aren’t we?

BEFORE THE KNOCKING, THERE WAS A COMPLICATED ROMANCE

At the centre of the affair was William Kent, a moneylender from Norfolk whose wife, Elizabeth Lynes, had died following childbirth. Their baby also died, leaving Kent bereaved.

Elizabeth’s sister, Frances, known as Fanny, helped with the household. She stayed, and a relationship developed between her and Kent.

Unfortunately, the church’s rules prevented them from marrying. Marrying your deceased wife’s sister was considered unacceptable, regardless of whether the two people involved actually wanted to do it.

After a period apart, William and Fanny reunited in London, living as husband and wife and making wills in each other’s favour. Her family disapproved. The couple needed somewhere discreet to live. Enter Richard Parsons.

A LANDLORD WITH AN UNSETTLING DEPOSIT SCHEME

Parsons, a parish clerk, offered the couple rooms in his house on Cock Lane. He had a wife, two daughters, a reputation for drinking and financial difficulties. Kent lent him twelve guineas, repayable in monthly instalments.

Oh, make a note of that loan. It will become rather more relevant than anything supposedly floating down the stairs.

The first disturbances were reported while Kent was away in the country. Fanny, then pregnant, was sharing a bed with Parsons’ young daughter Elizabeth when scratching and knocking sounds were heard.

At first, Mrs Parsons suggested a neighbouring cobbler was responsible. A perfectly reasonable explanation. At the time, London had far more people making shoes than people returning from the dead.

But the noises reportedly continued, and a local publican, James Franzen, claimed to have seen a white figure ascending the stairs. The house now had a haunting. And, as events would demonstrate, a landlord with considerable enthusiasm for developing it.

A DEATH THAT DESERVED BETTER

William and Fanny eventually moved out. In January 1760, Fanny became seriously ill. Her doctor and apothecary identified smallpox. She died on 2 February.

Before her death, she had ensured that Kent would inherit most of her estate. Her family’s objections, disputes over money and the precarious status of the couple’s relationship made an already painful situation more difficult.

Meanwhile, Parsons had failed to repay the full amount of Kent’s loan. Kent took legal action and recovered the outstanding debt by January 1762.

Around the same time, the mysterious noises at Cock Lane became a sensation. An unfortunate coincidence for Parsons but an exceptionally convenient one for the ghost.

ONE KNOCK FOR YES, TWO FOR CHARACTER ASSASSINATION

The disturbances now appeared to centre on Elizabeth Parsons. Her father enlisted the help of clergyman John Moore, and together they devised a way to question the supposed spirit.

One knock meant yes. Two meant no. We still use it [in 2026]. It’s a wonderfully efficient system.

The ghost was identified as Fanny. More importantly, it apparently claimed that she had been poisoned with arsenic by William Kent.

The doctors’ diagnosis of smallpox was suddenly competing with noises coming from a child’s bed. How this became a close contest is one of the story’s more unsettling aspects.

Moore took the allegations seriously. The Public Ledger published accounts of the haunting, and Kent found himself publicly suspected of murder. Albeit his accuser was a ghost.

PLEASE RESPECT THE GHOST’S TERMS AND CONDITIONS

Kent attended séances in an effort to clear his name, bringing along the medical men who had treated Fanny. The gatherings involved spectators clustered around Elizabeth’s bed while questions were put to the spirit. Participants were warned that the ghost was sensitive to disbelief.

A relative of Parsons, Mary Frazer, called repeatedly for Fanny to appear. At one gathering, when nothing happened, Moore suggested that the audience was making too much noise and sent them out. The ghost apparently needed a quieter environment in which to knock.

At another séance, an attempt to examine beneath the bed with a candle was met with the explanation that the spirit disliked light. It was remarkably particular for somebody who had supposedly travelled all the way back from the afterlife to expose a murderer.

When Kent asked whether he would be hanged, the spirit answered yes. He rejected it as a lying spirit, insisting that his Fanny would never have said such a thing.

THE MAID WAS HAVING NONE OF IT

One of the more refreshing figures in the affair was the couple’s former servant, Esther Carlisle, nicknamed “Carrots” because of her red hair.

Asked about Fanny’s supposed poisoning, she refused to support the accusation. She said William and Fanny had been loving and happy together.

During a séance, the spirit indicated that it was angry with her. Esther’s response was essentially that it ought to be ashamed of itself, because she had never harmed her mistress.

After so much solemn interpretation of scratching noises, somebody had finally told the ghost to stop being ridiculous. There is a great deal to be said for a witness who can look at an alleged supernatural manifestation and conclude that it needs a telling-off.

LONDON QUEUES FOR A LOAD OF OLD KNOCKS

By now, Cock Lane was attracting crowds large enough to obstruct the street. Parsons reportedly charged visitors to attend. The haunting had acquired a revenue stream.

Interest spread through the newspapers and into fashionable society. Horace Walpole and the Duke of York were among those drawn to the affair. A small bedroom had become London’s hottest attraction.

But doubts were growing. Attempts to observe Elizabeth more closely produced arguments, refusals and stretches of silence. At one examination, she admitted that she feared what would happen to her father if the haunting was exposed as a deception.

ENTER SAMUEL JOHNSON. EXIT THE GHOST.

A committee assembled to investigate included Samuel Johnson, the writer and formidable conversational presence.

Johnson was interested in the possibility of spirits. He also wanted evidence, an inconvenient requirement that can spoil a perfectly profitable haunting.

On 1 February 1762, the investigators gathered to examine the disturbances. Elizabeth was instructed to keep her hands outside the bed.

The promised supernatural activity failed to materialise. The spirit had also supposedly agreed to knock on Fanny’s coffin in the vault beneath St John’s Church, Clerkenwell. Members of the party went there to test the claim. Silence.

The committee concluded that the noises were being counterfeited by the child. Fanny, it appeared, had been credited with statements she had never made, delivered through a method she had never used.

THE AFTERLIFE, NOW AVAILABLE IN WOOD

Further examinations followed, and they were hardly gentle. Elizabeth was watched, moved between houses and subjected to tests. She was even threatened with imprisonment alongside her father if the noises failed to return.

She was a child surrounded by adults demanding a performance, then threatening punishment when they did not get one.

Eventually, attendants spotted her concealing a small piece of wood. Investigators concluded that she had been producing the scratches and knocks, under pressure from her father. The great mystery of Cock Lane had come down to a frightened girl and a bit of timber.

No gateway to another realm. No murdered woman seeking justice. Just adults who had built an enormous story around noises they were far too willing to interpret.

A HAUNTING WITH CONSEQUENCES

Kent pursued the people responsible for the accusations. In July 1762, Richard Parsons, his wife, Mary Frazer, John Moore and tradesman Richard James were tried for conspiracy and found guilty.

Moore and James later paid substantial compensation to Kent. Parsons received two years’ imprisonment and was ordered to stand in the pillory three times. His wife and Frazer also received prison sentences.

Curiously, the crowds treated Parsons sympathetically during his appearances in the pillory, even collecting money for him.

Having helped turn the affair into a public spectacle, London was apparently reluctant to lose a favourite performer.

Kent had faced a much uglier prospect: having his reputation destroyed by allegations supposedly delivered by the woman he had loved.

THE GHOST WENT QUIET. THE JOKES DIDN’T.

The Cock Lane affair lived on in satire, plays, prints and literature. William Hogarth mocked it. Charles Dickens later referred to it in his novels.

It also became tangled in religious disputes, with different groups arguing over what the haunting meant and whose beliefs it supported.

There is something horribly familiar about the whole business. An extraordinary claim gathers attention. Attention brings status, money and supporters. Questions become unwelcome. The accused struggles to be heard above people who have already decided.

Cock Lane managed all of this without a single Facebook group. Quite an achievement.

Beneath the ridiculous nickname and the crowded séances were a dead woman whose memory had been exploited, a man falsely accused of killing her, and a child pressed into keeping the performance going.

Fanny deserved to rest. Kent deserved to grieve. Elizabeth deserved adults who behaved better. Instead, London got a spectacle, and I got something to write about.

I have used GPT-6 Astra to decipher two Catholic League letters from 1593, written by Thibault Desportes, the secretary to the Duke of Mayenne.  To my knowledge, these letters have never been deciphered before.

Desportes wrote these letters to Pope Clement VIII's nephew Pietro Aldobrandini (who was responsible for French affairs in Rome) and to Mayenne's agent in Rome, Girolamo Frachetta, just as Mayenne's war against the Protestant French king Henry IV was beginning to unravel.  The letters were written 3 days before Henry converted to Catholicism in a bid to be recognized as the rightful ruler of France by the Pope and the French nobility.  (You may have heard the expression "Paris is well worthy of a Mass", which Henry allegedly offered as the reason for his conversion.)

In these letters, Desportes accuses the Pope of favoring Spanish interests over those of France and explains why a truce between the Catholic League (headed by Mayenne) and Henry IV would become inevitable following Henry IV's conversion.  Some really interesting details:

- Desportes names the exact price that Henry IV accepted to convert to Catholicism: 500,000 écus.

- Just two months after these letters were written, Frachetta betrayed Mayenne by handing over Desportes' correspondence to the Spanish ambassador.  These letters may explain why he did it: Desportes writes to Frachetta that Mayenne is unable to pay for Frachetta's services allegedly because funds for this payment had to come from a third party (a prelate) and "this is no time to take anything" from these funds.

- The letter to Frachetta reads like a piece of detective fiction, with elaborate code words used for names of various parties in Rome involved in an anti-Spanish conspiracy ("our friend at the college", "the man of La Chesne", "our uncle").

You can view the ciphers, their translations to French, and the translation from French to English (with significant historical notes included) at: https://t.co/4r3xrdb6ph

text:
Americans who are 65 or older but still working can continue using employer-sponsored insurance and are not required to switch to Medicare immediately; they should compare factors such as Part B and Part D premiums, IRMAA surcharges, and spousal coverage.

A *Wall Street Journal* report on the 1st noted that Americans who remain in the workforce after turning 65 often face a choice: continue with employer-provided health insurance or switch to Medicare. Employer-sponsored plans often feature lower premiums because the employer covers approximately 84% of the cost, whereas Medicare offers greater freedom in choosing doctors and carries a lower risk of unexpected medical bills. Notably, high-income workers must consider IRMAA surcharges, and if a 65-year-old worker switches to Medicare, a younger spouse might lose access to the workplace insurance plan.

However, turning 65 does not necessarily mean one must give up employer-provided health insurance in favor of Medicare.

Stephen Maggard, a financial planner in South Carolina, stated that many workers feel confused as they approach age 65 because they receive a flood of Medicare-related mail and assume they are required to make a change.

Unless a company has fewer than 20 employees, there is no mandate to switch primary insurance coverage to Medicare at age 65.

Workers at larger companies who are satisfied with their employer-sponsored health insurance can continue using their current plan until retirement—or switch to Medicare later if they determine it offers better value.

Financial experts advise workers to review their coverage options during the annual open enrollment period to ensure their preferred doctors, hospitals, and medications remain within the insurance network and that costs have not risen sharply.

Medicare consists primarily of three main parts:

*   Part A (Hospital Insurance)

Enrollment is free at age 65 or later, even if the individual also has employer-provided health insurance. * Part B: Medical Insurance

Part B serves as an alternative to employer-provided coverage, paying for expenses such as doctor visits, medical tests, and physical therapy.

* Part D: Prescription Drug Coverage

Government regulations require all individuals aged 65 or older who do not have "creditable" prescription drug coverage through their employer to enroll in Medicare Part D; failure to do so may result in a lifetime penalty.

This is long but worth the read, especially if you don't believe Trump hasn't accomplished anything.
Trump’s Top 25 Achievements: The List Every Conservative Should Know and Use
Donald Trump doesn’t have an accomplishment problem. Republicans have an information problem. It’s on each of us to change that.
With the midterms coming, an astonishing number of Republican voters cannot name three things President Trump has accomplished. Which is remarkable when you consider that Donald Trump has accomplished more in a year and a half than any other president ever did in four.
Indeed, he has accomplished so much, so fast, across so many fronts that most people cannot keep up. The Enemedia buries the victories, while Republicans do an abysmal job of explaining them.
So here is the cheat sheet. It barely scratches the surface. And yet each and every item here is a game-changer, and your befuddled black-pilling friends need to know it.
This is not a list of promises. It’s a list of laws enacted, cases won, policies implemented, agreements secured, and measurable results.
You don’t have to memorize all 25. Learn five. And when somebody says Trump “hasn’t done much,” show them the receipts.
Trump Restored American Safety and Sovereignty
1. He made the border a real border again.
In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.
2. He reversed mass migration.
America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”
Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.
3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.
Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.
Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.
4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.
According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.
This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.
Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle
5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.
The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.
Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.
6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one.
In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.
Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.
7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.
That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.
No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.
8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.
9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.
10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.
Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.
11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.
Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again
12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.
Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.
Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.
13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.
In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.
14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.
Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?
15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.
What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”
16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family
17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.
Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.
He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.
No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.
Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.
19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.
That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.
20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.
Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.
Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.
23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.
24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.
Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.
25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.
Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.
Now Act Like It Matters
Those are not tweets or campaign promises. They are changes in law, power, investment, sovereignty, culture, and the structure of the Republic itself. And they’re just the top 25: I could give you hundreds more.
Midterms are turnout elections. We do not need to convince Democrats to love Donald Trump. We need Republicans and friendly independents to understand what is at stake — and to show up.
And let’s be clear. When you say (as some of you will) “the Republicans need to do a good enough job telling this story”, you’re pointing at yourself. You are “the Republicans.” The Democrats don’t rely exclusively on their elected officials to tell their story: everyone from their media lackeys to their lowest-level supporters are constantly spreading their “news”, whatever that “news” happens to be.
Today’s conservatives have more ability to find whatever you want to know than any group of people in human history, yet half of them couldn’t name any of the accomplishments in this essay, and if they were to read it, they would just complain that something else they wanted hasn’t happened fast enough to suit them.
This is called “black-pilling.” It’s a loser mindset, and if you engage in it, you deserve to lose: horribly, painfully, personally. And guess what: you will, unless people who are serious step up to save you. Which is frankly pathetic, but for the rest of our sakes, necessary.
So tell people our story. Donald Trump is delivering great things, whether or not heaven on earth has broken out quite yet. Do the work, send the team he needs to Washington to finish the job, and get ready for 2028 afterward.
Take the time to learn at least five of these victories. Share this list with someone who needs it. And vote as though the most consequential Presidency in modern history depends on what you do.
Because it does.
Rod D. Martin

text:
Here are the three storylines that can each be stated without inventing facts.

The people walking. They left because wages and security at home were not enough, and a group is safer and cheaper than a smuggler. José Zelaya told EFE he wants to reach the U.S. so he can send money back; he named hunger and necessity, not a party, as the organizers. Others already stuck in Tapachula joined because Mexican paperwork was stalled. Some, like the Ecuadoran Vinicio Ogonaga, say Monterrey is the destination, not Texas. Cash help has been small and local: their own money, food from towns on the road, and about $100 from a Jesuit network in Guatemala. On this account the midterms are irrelevant. They are moving because the last place did not work.

The administration and most Republicans. The border is closed, releases have been at zero for 16 months, and this column will be stopped the same way. DHS and Secretary Mullin have said the group has no chance of entry; the White House told Newsweek illegal crossers will be arrested and removed. The political layer is a forecast, not a claim that the march is fake: migrants and smugglers watch U.S. politics, a Democratic Congress is widely expected to restrain ICE and widen asylum, and footage of people heading north is evidence that the incentive still exists. Nancy Mace’s version is the cleanest: they are not betting on crossing Trump’s border, they are betting on November. Credibility here depends on the enforcement record, which the administration can point to, not on proof that these 600 people are a coordinated invasion.

Democrats and the outlets covering it from the left. They have not offered a plan for this caravan, and the credible stance is that they do not need one yet. A few hundred people in Chiapas are a Mexican enforcement problem and a humanitarian footnote, not a U.S. border event. What they contest is the leap from that footage to “Democrats will open the border.” Their actual argument is about proportion and timing: the same images return before midterms, the group is a fraction of the 2018 caravans, and those were dispersed long before the Rio Grande. Greene’s “why now?” line is useful to them precisely because it comes from a Republican. The weak spot is silence. Refusing to say what should happen if the group does reach a port of entry leaves the forecast unchallenged.

All three can be true in part. The march does not require a U.S. campaign to explain it. The campaign does not require the march to be fake to use it. And a group this far south does not yet force a Democratic policy answer, which is why one has not appeared. The argument worth having is which of those claims is doing the real work.

text:
Not quite. The lawsuits alleged sexual assault and misconduct, but the NFL's own disciplinary officer found the league had not shown that he used physical force against the 4 therapists in its case, and she classified his conduct as non-violent. At the same time, no court has ever found him guilty of any crime. Grand juries in 2 Texas counties declined to indict him, which does not prove he is innocent. But his settlements are not an admission of guilt either. High-profile figures often settle simply to make the noise go away, not because they are conceding anything. The only formal finding was that he sexually assaulted those 4 therapists under the league's definition, and the NFL only has to find something more likely than not, a far lower bar than a criminal court.

The number of accusations is not proof of guilt either. It may be enough in the court of public opinion, but piling up public allegations is a familiar way to pressure someone with a lot of money, and a lot to lose, into settling. Gloria Allred's critics have long accused her of it, and I think Tony Buzbee was doing the same here. Not necessarily because he believed the women were lying, but because he wanted to win his case and was willing to let the chips fall where they may.

So you cannot call him a rapist as fact. I am seeing a lot of people do exactly that, and he was never even charged with it. I am just trying to offer a nuanced and objective perspective. No court has established that he is a rapist, an assaulter, or even that he committed misconduct. My guess is he is guilty of something, and it could be everything alleged. But it is also possible some of it was exaggerated for money. The record does not let anyone say which. We should not act as though we know. We can certainly be suspicious of bad behaviour.

Before all this, his record was seemingly spotless. He was well liked, he gave to charity, he carried himself well, and NFL teams vet closely before the draft. There is no public evidence he was anything but a decent person. Mike Tyson once said something to the effect that when you are favoured by God, you are also favoured by the devil. Maybe ego and temptation led him to do some very bad things. This is not an excuse, and I am not saying the therapists offered themselves. We do not know that. But successful, high-profile men often attract women who are willing to offer themselves freely. Very few men know what that is like. Women probably do, since they deal with that kind of attention all the time, famous or not. Still, I do not know whether any of that played a role.
But given that none of us actually knows what happened, as long as his behaviour is good moving forward, the rest is between him and God. You do not have to like him. But despising him and drawing harsh conclusions is not backed by fact. Only God knows what is in his heart.

Pulling the post and the record under it before writing the reinforcement. He was right when being right got you called a racist, and the record closed on his side.

In March 2006, Crystal Mangum accused three Duke lacrosse players, Reade Seligmann, Collin Finnerty, and David Evans, of rape at an off-campus party. Durham DA Mike Nifong, up for election, went on television and called them hooligans. Duke canceled the season. Faculty signed the Group of 88. The campus consensus was that the accusation was the verdict.

Stephen Miller was a Duke student. On August 28, 2006, he published “Persecution” in the Chronicle. He said the team was being railroaded, that the DNA was absent, that Nifong had invented a condom the accuser had already denied, and that the captains had offered to talk and take a polygraph. He said it on campus, and he said it on national television, when almost no other student would.

https://t.co/U7uPSwFdOJ

April 11, 2007, North Carolina Attorney General Roy Cooper dismissed every charge and did not stop at “insufficient evidence.” He declared the three innocent. He said there was no credible evidence an attack occurred in that house, called it a tragic rush to accuse, and called Nifong a rogue prosecutor.

https://t.co/Qu26KG461E

June 16, 2007, the State Bar disbarred Nifong. The panel found dishonesty, fraud, deceit, and misrepresentation. He had withheld exculpatory DNA, lied to the judge, and lied to investigators. The panel named political ambition as the motive.

Mangum was later convicted of second-degree murder in the 2011 stabbing of Reginald Daye and sentenced to 14 to 18 years. In December 2024, from the North Carolina Correctional Institution for Women, she admitted she had fabricated the rape allegation and asked the three men for forgiveness.

The only student willing to say the plain thing on a national camera was Stephen Miller. Eighteen years later, the accuser confessed, the prosecutor was disbarred, and the three men are innocent. That is not a vibe. That is the file.

NEW: Governor Mbah canvasses a nation that earns patriotism of the youth, makes ‘japa’ a choice

...As 2,101 corps members are sworn in in Enugu State

Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has charged Nigerians with collectively building a nation that earns the patriotism of young people, while also making migration a choice, not an escape route.

Mbah spoke in Awgu during the swearing-in ceremony for the 2026 Batch C Stream of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members deployed to Enugu State.

He stressed that Nigeria’s extraordinary youth population could only become a demographic dividend if the nation creates the education, skills, jobs, enterprise and institutions that enable young Nigerians to convert their energy and talent into productivity and prosperity, hence the essence of the NYSC beyond experiencing other parts of Nigeria.

“We often ask young Nigerians to be patriotic. But let us ask ourselves a more difficult question: How do we earn the patriotism of our young people if they feel excluded from their country's promise?

“Patriotism must be cultivated by creating a country in which young people can see a future for themselves.

“We must provide quality education; create an enabling environment for enterprise; expand opportunities; make our institutions work.

“We must build a country where merit is rewarded, hard work has meaning and dreams do not have to be exported before they can become reality,” he said.

Mbah, however, urged the youth to never forget the demands patriotism makes of them, both in good and difficult times.

“Patriotism also demands something from you. It demands that, even when the country is imperfect, you refuse to give up on its possibilities; that you criticise what is wrong without abandoning what can be made right; that you do not merely ask: ‘What can Nigeria give me?’

“but also ask: ‘What can I give Nigeria?’

“Together, we can build a country where ‘japa’ is a choice, not an escape; where our young people can travel the world without feeling compelled to abandon home.

“If you are called upon to teach, teach as though Nigeria’s future were sitting before you – because it is. And when you encounter the difficulties, do not simply ask: ‘When will Nigeria change?’ Ask the more powerful question: ‘What can I do to change Nigeria?’ That is the question of citizenship,” he emphasised.

He assured them of their welfare, safety and comfort in Enugu State, reminding them that Enugu is a state rich in cosmopolitan history, and where every citizen could attain any height he or she is capable of.

“The Government of Enugu State will continue to work with the NYSC authorities to provide a conducive, secure and supportive environment for your service. We will pay particular attention to your welfare, safety and the conditions under which you discharge your responsibilities across the state.

“But, importantly, note that you are not strangers in Enugu. Our history offers remarkable testimony. When Enugu was elevated to municipal status in 1952, Mallam Umaru Altine, a Fulani man from Sokoto, became its first Mayor.

“It tells us that in Enugu, where you come from need not determine how far you can go; that belonging is not always about birthplace; that citizenship is also about contribution,” he assured them.

Speaking earlier, the NYSC State Coordinator, Mrs. Oluwakemi Awolola, on behalf of the Director-General of the agency, Brigadier-General Olakunle Nafiu, said a total of 2,101 corps members had been registered under Batch C, and thanked Governor Mbah for improved welfare of Corps members and for making their environment conducive and safe.

“I am pleased to report that a total of 2,101 prospective corps members, comprising 983 males and 1,118 females, have been successfully registered for the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream/Orientation Course in Enugu State. Their level of cooperation, enthusiasm, and willingness to participate in camp activities have been commendable.

text:
The Threefold Social Order: Rudolf Steiner’s Path from Conflict to World Peace
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
World peace in this era cannot be secured by treaties alone.  Rudolf Steiner taught that peace has a social form, and that the form required now is the threefold social order.

Modern life, he said, has outgrown the habit of placing culture, rights, and the economy under a single power.  Each sphere has its own work.  When they are fused inside the national state, rivalry has a structure to grow in.  When they are distinguished, that structure weakens.

Culture(Liberty) Life
----------------------
Education, science, art, religion, and the free development of ideas - belongs to liberty.  Schools, research, and the arts serve peace when they are guided by those who practice them, and when they can cross borders without becoming instruments of the state or of economic interest.  A culture directed from above trains obedience.  A free cultural life trains the insight on which peace depends.

Political(Equality) Life
------------------------
The life of rights belongs to equality.  Law exists to protect persons, and every adult stands as an equal before it.  The state is necessary, and its task is limited.  It is not meant to manage production, and it is not meant to prescribe belief, science, or education.  Peace requires a rights-life that stops at the person, rather than a state that carries economic ambition and cultural domination into its dealings with other peoples.

Economic(Fraternity) Life
----------------------------
Economic life belongs to fraternity, understood as association.  Producers, traders, and consumers coordinate through agreements aimed at real needs.  Land and the means of production are administered so that people can work, rather than held as absolute private property in the old sense or absorbed by the state.  Rudolf Steiner held that wars are fed where economic advantage is pursued through national power.  An associative economy, organized around needs rather than national gain, removes that fuel.

Liberty, equality, and fraternity are thus given separate homes: liberty in culture, equality in rights, fraternity in the economy.  Rudolf Steiner did not offer this as a party program.  He asked schools, workshops, and associations to begin living it.

He tied the necessity of that beginning to this era.  People can no longer take their social order from inherited authority.  The same age that has made humanity one economic and legal world has also made conscious insight the only reliable basis of common life.  Without the threefold order, the mixing of power, culture, and profit continues, and with it the conditions of war.  With it, peace has a structure to stand on.

The same mixing of powers shows itself in the wars and standoffs of the present.  In Ukraine, Gaza, and the wider contests among great powers, legal authority, economic interest, and cultural or religious claim are carried by the same national hand: territory is pursued as security, resources and trade routes as national advantage, and belief or historical narrative as a warrant for force.  Rudolf Steiner’s threefold order answers that pattern directly.  A rights-life limited to the equality of persons would take conquest and collective punishment off the table; an economy of associations, aimed at needs rather than strategic gain, would loosen the hold of fuel, grain, arms, and shipping lanes as reasons for war; a free cultural life would keep schools, churches, and the telling of history from becoming instruments of the state.  Applied in that way, the threefold order does not dissolve any present conflict overnight. It names the social form in which those conflicts lose their reason to continue, and in which peace can be built by separating what the warring states have fused.

text:
A college can buy an AI tutor without getting much tutoring.

In a new Maryland working paper, only about 15% of students offered a course-specific assistant used it. The researchers found lower grades when comparing sections of the same course. That deserves attention, but it doesn’t show that the students who used AI learned less. Three instructors were also excluded after randomization, so even the rollout comparison needs caution.

StudentBench studied a different setting: adults were paid to complete an hour of tutoring, then took an unaided test. AI tutoring beat the control among the participants retained in the analysis. But sessions with very little AI participation were excluded, and the control watched unrelated educational videos rather than doing an hour of ordinary test practice.

For a school choosing an AI product, access and usage aren’t minor implementation details. They determine who the promised benefit can reach. Evidence from engaged participants cannot answer what a whole class will gain from being offered a tool.

Both papers leave the longer-term question open: what will students retain and apply when the assistant is gone?

#Eritrea's Delegation led by Foreign Minister Osman Saleh met, yesterday in Washington, with US Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, Ms. Allison Hooker, and, the Assistant Secretary for Africa, Mr. Frank Garcia ,respectively.

In the meeting with the Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, Minister Osman welcomed the removal of unilateral sanctions which must be seen as a positive and vital step for turning a new page in Eritrea-US relations.  

Eritrea's objective is to create the basis for constructive, mutually beneficial, and genuine partnership in the period ahead.  The new chapter should enable us to recoup missed opportunities;  pivot towards enhancement of trade and investment; as well as explore and leverage new prospects for genuine partnership that eschews structural dependency, FM Osman stressed. 

Minister Osman also referred to the need for further review of unwarranted policies of pressure pursued by previous Administrations.  He elaborated on Eritrea's modest and constructive role in the promotion of peace, stability and security in its immediate and wider neighborhood which encompasses the Horn of Africa; the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden; the Nile Basin, and the Wider Gulf Region.  The Minister expressed Eritrea's earnest hope to cultivate collaborative efforts with the US in these ideals as well as in the mechanism of cooperation charted out by the littoral States.  

The Under Secretary for Political Affairs, for her part, underlined that the lifting of sanctions stemmed from President Trump's commitment to nurture bilateral partnerships based on mutual benefits.  This will contribute to the crystallization of warm ties of cooperation between the two countries.  Ms. Hooker further remarked on the broad convergence of broad themes of cooperation envisaged by the two sides in these initial and preliminary meetings.

The meeting with the Assistant Secretary State, Mr. Frank Garcia, was likewise focused on broadly similar themes.  The two sides agreed that future talks will focus on more profound and concrete consultations for the promotion of trade and investment; regional peace and stability, as well as resolution of pending matters through constructive dialogue.

Washington, D.C.

A local resident witnessed a massive multi-agency law enforcement operation unfold through a residential neighborhood during afternoon school pick-up hours.

According to the eyewitness account, more than 25 officers and federal agents operating at least 15 vehicles converged on the area to apprehend a single individual. The response drew from five distinct agencies: the DEA, FBI, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the D.C. Metropolitan Police Department, and the U.S. Park Police.

The observer reported that the operation involved a coordinated, high-speed vehicle pursuit through neighborhood streets, with enforcement vehicles blowing through stop signs at dangerous speeds while parents and children were actively navigating school dismissals. Compounding the confusion, officials on scene offered conflicting explanations for the mobilization—DEA personnel reportedly cited a narcotics investigation, while HSI stated it was connected to a hit-and-run incident.

When authorities finally stopped the individual, the witness noted he offered no physical resistance to arrest, experienced a medical episode on site, and was subsequently transported away in an ambulance. Calling the mobilization an obscene display of over-policing that endangered innocent bystanders, the resident maintained that the incident solidified their support for the "Defund the Police" and "Abolish ICE" movements.

text:
Baghdad announces a U.S. waiver for Najaf flights: forty Iranian services a day, Mahan left out

The office of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi said on Friday, October 2, 2026, that an agreement allows Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate forty flights a day to and from Najaf International Airport. Al-Zaidi thanked what he called the U.S. government’s positive response and its cooperation in granting the requested exemption.

From suspension to waiver

Iraq halted flights to and from Iran last week in line with U.S. sanctions, after the Treasury on September 8 imposed restrictions on dozens of Iranian carriers and firms that service them. On September 29 the first waiver covered only Iraqi Airways, while Iranian carriers remained barred from Iraqi airports. Friday’s statement extends the exception to Iranian airlines and limits it to Najaf. Reuters reported on September 28, citing a person familiar with the talks, that the administration was moving toward a one-month waiver for pilgrim flights between Iran and Najaf, with a longer waiver possible later. Al-Zaidi’s statement did not set the duration of the new exemption or the date it takes effect.

Why Najaf, and why Mahan was excluded

Najaf is the city of Imam Ali’s shrine and a main artery for religious visits, medical travel and cross-border tourism. The media office said the follow-up was meant to ease the movement of travelers and pilgrims and to support humanitarian, medical, tourism and educational needs, and that al-Zaidi held a series of contacts with the parties concerned. Al Hurra, citing an Iraqi Foreign Ministry source, reported that the waiver followed a Sunday call in which the prime minister asked U.S. envoy Tom Barrack to exempt Najaf airport. Mahan’s exclusion has a stated American basis: Washington accuses the carrier of transporting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps personnel, weapons and drones. According to a Reuters source on the earlier waiver talks, al-Zaidi offered safeguards including screening and information sharing, and a bar on using the flights to move weapons, sanctioned individuals or illicit funds.

The limit of the waiver

The opening remains partial. Iranian flights are still suspended at other airports, including Baghdad, Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, Euronews reported, citing the Iraqi News Agency. The exception is a conditional U.S. license, not a lifting of sanctions on Iran’s aviation sector. It is also a test for Baghdad: a balance between Washington’s pressure and the needs of millions of pilgrims and patients, on an air corridor that has become a political file as much as a humanitarian one.

His "Vitale-isms" have taken on a life of their own, with "Awesome, baby!," "Get a T.O., baby!", "PTP'er" (primetime player), M&M'er (a mismatch), "Diaper Dandy" (freshman star), and many more all becoming part of the vernacular. Along with so many tremendous moments on camera, there's also been Vitale's devotion to fighting cancer, well before he was stricken with the disease, a passion originally ignited by his dear friend, college basketball coach Jim Valvano. Vitale's focus has long been fighting pediatric cancer in particular, and he has helped raise tens of millions of dollars for the cause. The timing of the film is especially poignant considering the 83-year-old Vitale's recent battle with cancer, and his upcoming honor at the ESPYS as the recipient of the Jimmy V Award for Perseverance.

text:
$BLLN: I think I found my next >20 bagger

Many of you know that I’m a very concentrated investor. 

I went very heavy into $HIMS at $6-12 and then shortly thereafter into $IREN sub $5, with an average price of about $7.50.

Today, I’m still pretty much all-in $IREN since I think the stock has yet to reach its full potential, with plenty of gains still to be had.

That said, I’m always on the lookout for my next big “bet,” which prompted me to launch our Radar Report series on Substack and X.

The goal of the series is to explore stocks that are still flying under the radar and figure out whether any of them have a realistic chance of becoming major multibaggers.

The stocks I’ve deep dived on so far as part of the series:

$GROY / $REAX / $PGY / $SLDE / $BLLN

I might end up investing in each one of those in the future given their potential, but the one I’m most excited about is $BLLN, the most recent company we covered in a new Radar Report released yesterday.

There are certain companies that eventually become almost synonymous with the industry they dominate. Electric cars make people think of $TSLA, smartphones of $AAPL, while $NVDA has become the defining name in AI hardware.

I think early cancer detection could eventually have a name attached to it as well, and from everything I have seen so far, BillionToOne has a serious chance of becoming that company.

Before I explain why, this is not one of those biotech moonshots that spends hundreds of millions of dollars every year hoping that one experimental drug eventually makes it through clinical trials.

$BLLN is already a profitable diagnostics company with an established prenatal business, 22 consecutive quarters of revenue growth and another major business in oncology that is still in the early stages of scaling.

The technology behind all of this came from founders Oguzhan Atay and David Tsao, both of whom distinguished themselves at Princeton before pursuing doctoral work at Stanford and Rice. What they eventually built is surprisingly elegant for something that solves such a difficult problem.

Genetic testing requires DNA to be copied before it can be properly analyzed, yet that copying process distorts the original quantities because some fragments get duplicated more than others. 

$BLLN figured out a way to measure that distortion and mathematically subtract it afterward, allowing the company to count incredibly small quantities of DNA with a level of precision that conventional methods struggle to achieve.

That sounds more complicated than it actually is in practice, and we break the mechanism down much more clearly in the full report.

In any case, the same basic idea is now being applied across several completely different markets.

$BLLN started in prenatal testing because it offered the quickest route to an established business.

Its UNITY platform can use an ordinary blood draw from the mother to screen the baby for genetic conditions that competing prenatal tests either cannot detect directly or struggle to detect with the same approach, which helped the company build its way to roughly 20% of pregnancies that actually undergo prenatal screening in the US.

The company then took essentially the same technology into oncology, because tumor DNA floating through a cancer patient’s bloodstream presents a very similar problem. The signal is tiny, surrounded by an enormous amount of normal DNA, yet finding and accurately measuring that signal can tell an oncologist which mutations are driving the cancer and whether a treatment is actually working.

The next step is MRD, or minimal residual disease, where $BLLN wants to detect microscopic traces of cancer left behind after surgery before they grow large enough to become visible on a scan. That product is expected to launch around the end of this year and moves the company one step closer to the market I find most interesting of all.

Early cancer detection.

Cancer would be a very different problem if a routine blood test could find a tumor while it was still at stage 1, when it is small, localized and in many cases still removable through surgery. The problem today is that these tumors shed almost no DNA into the bloodstream, while a screening test used on millions of healthy people also needs to avoid false alarms with extraordinary accuracy.

Nobody has properly solved both sides of that equation yet...

There is obviously a lot more to the story than what I’ve laid out here. In the full Radar Report, I go much deeper into the technology, business model, competitive landscape, regulatory environment, risks, valuation and the different markets $BLLN is ultimately trying to attack.

After spending the last few weeks researching the company from pretty much every angle I could think of, I genuinely believe this could become a >$100B company over time. At a market cap of ~$5B today, the potential upside for shareholders is enormous if that thesis proves right.

I’m not personally invested yet, since most of my capital remains concentrated in $IREN and I still think there is a major re-rating ahead there. But once that happens, $BLLN is currently the company I’m most seriously considering for my next major position.

If I eventually make that move, I’ll start covering the company on an ongoing basis, both publicly here on X and in considerably more depth for subscribers.

The full Radar Report, BLLN: Genomic’s Disruptive Dark Horse, is available to all X subscribers and Advanced+ subscribers on Substack.

Links to the full report in the comments below.

Wishing you all a great weekend! ✌️

text:
#PanCANvolunteer and pancreatic cancer survivor Diane B. shares: "On August 8, 2006, my three adult children joined me as we drove up to Stanford Hospital for my Whipple procedure. I wasn’t very concerned because my surgeon, Dr. Jeffrey Norton, now retired, had said, “Don’t worry — you’ll be fine. I’ve done hundreds of these.” So, I wasn’t (very worried).

Nine days later when I was home and checking the internet I saw that the five-year survival rate for pancreatic cancer was 5% (in 2006). My biggest hope was that my two grandchildren (and those to come in the future) would remember me, as I remember my grandparents.

After about 10 days, I began my 6-month chemo treatment followed by scans and blood work for five years. I’ve never had a recurrence.

I allowed myself a year to feel truly 'normal' again and that’s when I learned about PanCAN and began volunteering. Through donating, advocating and fundraising, PanCAN has given me the opportunity to participate in the increased hope being offered to those who are diagnosed. Yes, daraxonrasib is amazing and so is immunotherapy but PanCAN has been there for 25 years offering hope and help to those diagnosed and offering financial grants, encouragement and leadership to young researchers.

On August 8, 2026, my children and seven of my eight grandchildren joined me in Yosemite to celebrate my 20th Whipple anniversary. And I learned that we were celebrating something else too — Carmen, my granddaughter, is pregnant! Now I have a new wish: that my great-grandchildren will remember me.”

Join us in celebrating Diane's 20 years of survivorship in the comments. 💜

Introducing our State of Markets pt 2, along with a companion podcast where we unpack the data and discuss what comes next.

Tech is the everything cycle.

Supply: putting the buildout in context, just passed railroads as % of GDP. The wisdom of Elon is real: the factory (or the datacenter!) is the product.
